data.title: Students join Yellow Vest protest: Greater collective strength versus risk of losing distinct voice

data.title: Midterms 2026: Can Democrats capitalise on Latino voter regret?
data.description: In 2024, a 46 percent share of the Latino vote helped propel Donald Trump to the White House. But two years on, polls show that support has plummeted in spectacular fashion. Amid an immigration crackdown, violent ICE raids and the spiraling cost of living, some Latino voters say they regret having backed Trump at the ballot box. Now, as the midterms approach, can the Democrats capitalise on this sense of regret to win back what was once an essential part of their base? France 24 reporters Sam Ball and Barbara Gabel met with Latino voters and local Democrats in Phoenix, Arizona, to find out.

data.title: UK bookstores scramble as Sally Rooney's novels are pulled over Palestine Action support
data.description: Critically acclaimed Irish novelist Sally Rooney's announcement that her books could no longer be sold in the UK due to her support for proscribed group Palestine Action has left British booksellers rushing to stock up on her works before distributors run out. The British government's ban on the group, which practiced non-violent direct action and sabotage against UK military assets believed to be working with the Israeli government, makes support for Palestine Action punishable by up to 14 years in prison.

data.title: Oxfam takes France to court over 'tax inequality': 'Problem' with tax system, public service funding
data.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Layla Abdelké Yakoub, Tax Justice and Inequality Advocacy Officer at Oxfam France. "Today in France a billionaire pays less taxes proportionally than a nurse or a firefighter," explains Yakoub. She challenges the foundations of France's fiscal system, arguing that the growing concentration of wealth and preferential tax treatment of the ultra-rich are undermining the constitutional principle of equality before taxation. As Oxfam pursues legal action against the French state, Yakoub describes a widening disconnect between the government's efforts to attract investment and its ability to finance public services, address poverty and carve out an ecological transition.

data.title: Fake AI images of protester go viral after woman punched at Trump's Ohio rally
data.description: A protester who heckled Donald Trump at his midterm rally in Youngstown, Ohio, was physically assaulted and removed from the event, but fake AI-generated photos recreating the incident are going viral online. While footage confirms the woman was punched, there is no evidence to support Trump’s claim that the protester was "paid" to disrupt his speech, as he mocked the protester's weight. Vedika Bahl explains in Truth or Fake.

data.title: ‘People’s dignity, and democracy, is at stake’: meet the economist ditching ideology for reality
data.description: Exclusive: Isabella Weber prescribes a common-sense solution to poverty, inequality and fascism – making life’s essentials affordable for all The trouble with economists, Isabella Weber believes, is they do not behave like dentists. They obsess over ideological purity and are inflexible when searching for solutions, regardless of society’s symptoms. Dentists have no such pretensions – patients have little patience for dogma when in insufferable pain. John Maynard Keynes, Weber clarifies in the canteen of the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (Berlin’s Institute for Advanced Study), was the first to draw this dental comparison – and she is running with it. As she sees it, the symptoms could not be more severe. “The status quo for the majority is entirely unbearable,” while extreme inequality and corporate concentration has reached levels “simply incompatible with democracy” worldwide. This is exacerbated by a climate crisis that “generates massive windfall profits” for big business as the “ecological foundations of our lives disintegrate”. All the while the far right is making hay. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I need to prove my family’s sacrifice was worth it’: how pop auteur Shygirl slogged her way to the top
data.description: Adored by Madonna and Charli xcx and buoyed by finding true love, the Londoner is branching out into rock and breaking the mainstream. She explains how her working class upbringing made her so fearless Leaving the important stuff to chance isn’t Shygirl’s style. First aid kit, wind-up radio, batteries: earlier this morning, the singer filled her online shopping basket in preparation for impending disaster. She had read a news article advising households to put together an emergency kit. “I’m that kind of person,” she says, grinning. She woke her boyfriend, who was asleep in bed next to her. “I was like: babe, we’re sorted! I’ve got the water purifying tablets, everything!” It’s a sticky September afternoon in east London, and the singer, whose real name is Blane Muise, introduces herself as “Shy” and slides into the booth opposite me at an Italian trattoria. She first burst on to the club scene with the naughty, pulsating Want More in 2016, and in the decade since, the singer, rapper and DJ has applied the same rigour to her career as she has to her emergency prepping, going from cult underground artist to rising pop star, opening arenas for Beyoncé and Charli xcx, winning a Mobo award in 2024, and appearing in Madonna’s recent Confessions II – The Film, in which she shared a toilet stall with Arca and Richard E Grant. Continue reading...

data.title: Like dinosaur eggs in the sand: the pterosaur museum built to thrive in the Gobi desert
data.description: How architects worked with harsh environment to create sustainable building in location where fossils were found Viewed from afar, the silver-hued Hami Pterosaur Museum almost looks like a space base on Mars. Viewed from above, it resembles a collection of dinosaur eggs in the sand. Nestled in the Gobi desert, in north-west China, the new tourist attraction showcases hundreds of impressive fossils of pterosaurs, ancient flying reptiles related to dinosaurs. But far from reflecting its prehistoric exhibits, the building itself is a modern-day architectural specimen. Designed with underground exhibition halls, giant light funnels and sprawling solar farms, the museum is able to operate sustainably while withstanding an extremely harsh environment. Continue reading...

data.title: Revealed: VW, Ford and Tesla batteries linked to destructive deforestation of indigenous lands
data.description: Mines in supply chains of western carmakers linked to widespread deforestation of primary rainforest in nickel-rich lands inhabited by Tolaki people in Indonesia Volkswagen, Ford and Tesla are among the electric carmakers whose batteries may contain nickel mined in indigenous woodlands plagued by deforestation, an analysis has found, highlighting the struggle to make vehicles that are free from environmental destruction. Corporate disclosures and trade flows from the last two years show mines in the battery supply chains of automotive giants are linked to the loss of trees in Sulawesi, a wildlife hotspot in Indonesia that houses the world’s largest nickel deposits. The metal is widely used in cathodes in car batteries because it boosts energy density and increases range. Continue reading...

Across 53 towns and 96 cinemas, the film reportedly pulled in over 40,000 viewers in a single night, a number arthouse cinema rarely sees in Romania. data.title: Calling the shots: what NAZA says about perpetrator cinema
data.description: The documentary detailing Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza is the latest film to give a voice to those who carry out atrocities – confronting viewers with some of the most difficult questions of all Are we still talking about the banality of evil? When that overworked phrase was first used by philosopher Hannah Arendt, it described the blank persona of Nazi war criminal Adolf Eichmann. Now, in NAZA , anonymised members of Israeli intelligence discuss their remote execution of the assault on Gaza. The comparison to Hitler’s Germany, while understandably controversial, is made by a subject themselves. If they are banal, it is a modern, oddly familiar kind. These are articulate, middle-class millennials. They say they are leftwing and non-racist. Put differently, they could be Guardian readers. And yes, one remarks , they have been conducting a genocide. Continue reading...

data.title: Make Me Well by Xand van Tulleken – an eye-opening takedown of wellness myths
data.description: The engaging TV doctor dismantles the spurious science behind modern day snake oils, from collagen to turmeric When Xand van Tulleken set off on a journey into the wild west of wellness, he didn’t expect to discover anything new about vitamin D. Of all the supplements that line our shelves and social media feeds, it ought to be the least controversial; even the NHS website, which is hardly a wellspring of quackery, advises that everyone should consider taking a daily dose during autumn and winter, when we risk becoming deficient (D is the vitamin we get mostly from sunlight, and which helps keep our bones strong). The tiggerish TV doctor and twin brother to Chris (he’s the one who wrote Ultra-Processed People about the food industry) qualified at a time of high excitement in vitamin D circles; in the early 2000s, big studies were linking it not just to bone health but cancer, heart disease and dementia. “The range of potential problems to be solved was dizzying,” Van Tulleken writes in Make Me Well. data.title: AI threatens democracy. But we are not powerless: here’s how to fight back | Carine Fouteau
data.description: Tech platforms pillage public-interest journalism for profit. But we have leverage as they sow the seeds of their own downfall Carine Fouteau is president and publishing director of the French investigative news outlet Mediapart Big tech companies pose an immeasurable threat: socially, politically, militarily and ecologically. They are also causing a profound crisis of information. The tools they design now serve as weapons of mass destruction against democracy. There is so much at stake that an urgent and broad mobilisation is required. From the harvesting of personal data and the weaponisation of public opinion, to the destruction of jobs, the infringement of civil liberties and environmental damage, ordinary citizens are the main victims of this predatory economy – an economy with an agenda that aligns with the interests of the planet’s most authoritarian and reactionary states. data.title: It’s not the old two-party politics – but Labour and the Tories now know they can shun their populist challengers | Gaby Hinsliff
data.description: Though Burnham and Badenoch may still need the votes of Green and Reform supporters, both leaders have drawn clear lines in the sand Ask a straight question, get a straight answer. It’s how politics is supposed to work but almost never does, which is why on the rare occasions it happens the result can be faintly chaotic. What did Andy Burnham mean when he said – in response to a question from the Tory MP Harriett Baldwin – that Labour couldn’t partner with the Green party while it remains wedded to the “Zionism is racism” motion its members have just endorsed? Were Green MPs now barred from a future coalition government? If so, what about councils where they are currently sharing power with Labour? Though Burnham was only confirming what ministers have been arguing privately for days, at first nobody seemed to know: tellingly, it took almost 24 hours for the Labour party chair, Bridget Phillipson, to confirm that unless local Green groups disowned that idea sharpish, “Labour will bring any such local arrangement to an end”. So much for cuddly cross-party Andy, who always seemed so relaxed about rainbow coalitions. Now elected Greens in places such as Sheffield or Lewes must choose between power and members’ wrath, a useful rehearsal for what a hung parliament might feel like. Continue reading...

data.title: Britain is addicted to prisons. Our crumbling probation service proves they don’t work | Polly Toynbee
data.description: The current system is unable to quench the public thirst for locking people up – and certainly doesn’t ensure proper care once they are released Public services need more investment across the board. Every day, another wretched story. Look at the Institute for Government’s (IFG) Public Services Performance Tracker for a plain assessment of A&E corridor care, councils struggling to meet the demands of social care and the Send system, the courts backlog, GP caseloads or families lost in temporary accommodation. A chancellor approaching a budget is besieged by need. It’s easy for us journalists to pick out shock stories and claim each one is an absolute priority, but how should a chancellor choose? I’d like to draw attention to the probation officers, whose conference in Newcastle is launching a ballot for industrial action. Their caseloads overflowed long ago, but now thousands of prisoners released early – 2,000 this month – have been thrust upon them. The responsibility is overwhelming, with officers blamed for crimes their clients commit. Polly Toynbee is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The right’s scrounger rhetoric dominates the benefits debate. Labour must fight back – and win | Frances Ryan
data.description: The prime minister has a once-in-a-generation chance to reintroduce compassion to welfare. He has to seize the moment Back in 2009, months before the coalition government unleashed sweeping austerity, the then Conservative backbencher Iain Duncan Smith produced a study that would go on to lay the foundations for the rollout of universal credit. Now, nearly two decades later, Duncan Smith and his thinktank, the Centre for Social Justice (CSJ), has published State of Dependency: a landmark report promising to expose “the full scale of Britain’s worklessness crisis”. The study paints a picture of mass benefits reliance: it identifies 3,400 local areas where more than half the working-age population are on out-of-work benefits, or “economic opiates”, as the authors call them. They’ve even provided an interactive map (in the yellow and black colours of a road hazard sign, no less) so members of the public can type in their postcode to see if their neighbourhood is “a welfare hotspot”. Frances Ryan is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: Sally Rooney’s stand on Palestine is brave and humane
data.description: The Normal People author’s determination to support Palestine Action, even if it means that her books are withdrawn from sale in the UK, makes a mockery of Britain’s terrorism laws It’s hard to think of a published author in living memory who risked arrest in the UK for their political beliefs, hard to think of one whose books could be published anywhere but here. Sally Rooney went into this debacle with her eyes open: she said last July that royalties from her books, and their BBC adaptations, would be used to support Palestine Action. Rooney’s courage is not so much in risking imprisonment , since there is a fix for that, which is what she’s doing – avoiding the UK. Rather, she has chosen the thorniest possible path for this cause. Authors can write essays and sign letters in support of the Palestinian people; actors can voice it in interviews, musicians can say it from the stage, and there is always a cost to it, whether it’s in plain sight and they’ve been kicked off a global tour, or it’s behind closed doors and they are simply excluded from opportunities. But such actions, even if they logically suggest support for a proscribed organisation, don’t entail actively breaking the terrorism laws. Rooney had taken a financial hit anyway, by pledging support for Palestine Action with her royalties; but that’s a price at least you can count. The lost sales and opportunities that ripple out from being effectively both barred from and banned in the UK are innumerable. Continue reading...

data.title: Evanilson, Rayan and Rodríguez goals seal Bournemouth’s historic home win in Europe
data.description: An impossible dream realised: the Vitality Stadium staging European football, where the Europa League is becoming an oasis for Bournemouth. No wins yet in the Premier League, but beating Sturm Graz following up winning away at Real Sociedad should calm the domestic pressures mounting on Marco Rose. A pair of Brazilians secured club history, with Evanilson’s first-half header followed by Rayan’s later drive, a clincher coming just as the Austrian visitors were pushing hard for an equaliser. Álvaro Rodríguez’s stoppage-time penalty extended the celebrations. Flag day at the Vitality. Elvis Presley’s high baritone and Andy Williams’ tenor on the public address system marked a different type of occasion. Bournemouth have come a significant distance. “Minus 17 to European dreams” read a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand, marking the journey from the foot of the Football League to becoming a model, continental club. Milan visit next week, an occasion to further broaden the smile of Bill Foley, Bournemouth’s financier present in the posh seats. “A long time coming,” said Bournemouth’s long-serving captain, Adam Smith. “The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.” Continue reading...

data.title: From Dallaglio’s medals to Cantona’s shorts, sporting memorabilia is big business | Emma John
data.description: Like transfer fees and ticket prices, mementoes are one more marker of sport’s rampant self-inflation The auctioneer cradled his gavel in his palm like a pipe, the handle pointing towards him. It gave his patter the air of a Victorian gentleman holding forth by the mantelpiece in a period drama. “Are you bidding, Wilf? You’re waving at me.” Under the hammer was a Barclays Manager of the Month trophy, complete with travel case, but no indication of which Premier League luminary once owned it. It outstripped its estimate and sold for £700. An hour and a half into what Budds auction house dubbed its “Octoberfest” of sporting memorabilia, David Convery at the podium showed no sign of fatigue, save the occasional swig from a water bottle. There were 332 lots in total; Convery regularly manages sales with twice as many. In his three decades as an auctioneer he’s even secured some world-record prices, from the oldest surviving FA Cup to Pelé’s 1970 World Cup final shirt. Continue reading...

data.title: The hidden costs of fracking: boom in Argentina linked to trail of sickness
data.description: Families in Vaca Muerta, the centre of Patagonia’s shale operation, report cancers, miscarriages and pollution In Allen, a small town in Argentine Patagonia, many people living on the same street ended up falling ill. For some, it was severe migraines, nausea or skin irritation. For others, cancers, congenital abnormalities, miscarriages or stillbirth seemed to affect foetuses or children. People say it all started 13 years ago – when a well was drilled near their homes to extract gas and oil. Calle Ciega 10 [Dead-end Street 10] lies on the eastern edge of Vaca Muerta, a vital area for Argentina ’s economy, home to the world’s second-largest reserve of shale gas and fourth-largest reserve of shale oil. The region has more than 2,600 active wells , including one on this small street where about 20 families live, most of them seasonal workers on fruit farms. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Like selling wolves from Yellowstone’: how protected US sharks are being sold off to foreign aquariums
data.description: While anglers cannot take endangered sand tiger sharks, a loophole lets private firms catch the fish to sell abroad, profiting from Delaware Bay’s conservation success Shortly after 12.45pm, what remains of a 300-metre line goes taut. Somewhere beneath the murky green surface of Delaware Bay, on the eastern US coast, a sand tiger shark has taken the bait of a mackerel chunk. Marine researchers at the University of Delaware haul the line towards a small boat as the shark’s grey-brown outline emerges. It is a large animal: 225cm (7ft) long with a 90cm girth. Its mouth hangs open, revealing rows of jagged teeth. The researchers work quickly, measuring the shark, recording its sex, and taking blood and muscle samples. A tag is then fastened beneath its dorsal fin, through its thick sandpapery skin. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘She asked me to lie on her feet while she did sit-ups’: your memories of Esther Rantzen
data.description: From inspiring careers to treating people to unforgettable curries, the late presenter and campaigner had quite the impact on Guardian readers. Colleagues, admirers and TV show guests share their stories The summer of 1976 held a particularly fond memory for my family. In one episode of her programme The Big Time, my father took part in conducting the Royal Philharmonic in Croydon and met several of his musical idols. Esther and her team visited our home, causing much teenage excitement, took us for lunch at a local Indian restaurant (the height of sophistication) and after lunch asked me to sit on her feet in our back garden while she did sit-ups. We were kids, probably in the way of filming, but were included and treated warmly and impressed by her down-to-earth manner. data.title: Your full attention: Jesse Eisenberg’s 10 best film performances – ranked!
data.description: As his new movie The Debut closes the London film festival, we count down the best of the actor’s shy, sly and sometimes hairy outings A doppelganger role can be a trap for an actor: either the two roles are not sufficiently distinct, or they are too hammily different, and either way the result can look like a film school graduation project. But Jesse Eisenberg gives a stylish split-personality turn in Richard Ayoade’s adaptation of the Dostoevsky novella. He plays Simon, a nerdily shy and self-effacing computer programmer in a grim futureworld, ignored by his employers and by co-worker Hannah (Mia Wasikowska), with whom he is hopelessly in love. But then his carbon copy, James, arrives, also of course played by Eisenberg. James is a confident alpha-achiever who impresses his bosses and entrances Hannah – to Simon’s gibbering despair. data.title: Whalefall review – slimy survival thriller traps us in a whale and struggles to make it digestible
data.description: Austin Abrams gets eaten by a sperm whale in an overlong and flashback-heavy adaptation of Daniel Kraus’s hit novel that only has us on edge in moments Spare a thought for poor Austin Abrams, who, having just endured the world’s worst, and gloopiest, courier assignment in Resident Evil , has now been trapped inside a sperm whale … The immensely likable Euphoria alum (has any show in recent memory provided quite as many genuine stars?) brings what he can to Brian Duffield’s rather soggy adaptation of Pulitzer prize-winner Daniel Kraus’s acclaimed novel Whalefall. But there’s not a great deal he can do, despite being in every scene of what’s his second studio lead in a month, other than scream and writhe and look understandably alarmed. It’s a setup that’s grabby enough to have us wonder just how the hell it’s going to play out (what if that one scene in Finding Nemo but a whole movie) but it just doesn’t work as a 106-minute adventure, too overstretched and too silly to have us rooting for his escape and caring how he might orchestrate it. data.title: Worldpeace DMT: Stick Around for Tea review – ‘laptop twee’ duo keep things goofy but strengthen songs
data.description: (WPDMT) Bringing back the hyperliterate sound design of their acclaimed 2025 debut, the London duo explore childhood with whimsical humour and terrific musicality One of last year’s surprise highlights was The Velvet Underground & Rowan, the debut album by the wacky, hyperliterate London duo Worldpeace DMT. That irreverent album title summed up their approach to their references: Leo Fincham and Rowan Miles – also of the Femcels – buttressed nods to Fleetwood Mac and the Beach Boys with a palette straight out of NME circa 2011. If it isn’t a coup to make the sound of Grouplove and Darwin Deez sound cool and urbane in 2025, I don’t know what is. This year, Worldpeace DMT have changed tack, perhaps in response to suggestions that they’re at the forefront of an emergent genre called “ laptop twee ”. The duo’s August mixtape Flowers Powers mostly eschewed plunderphonics and heavy sampling in favour of live instrumentation that ran the gamut from Spiritualized to outlaw country; Stick Around for Tea, their second album, brings back a shade of the goofy, Sung Tongs -esque sound design that made their debut such a joy, while pulling Fincham and Miles’ songwriting to the fore. Stick Around for Tea seems, loosely, to be a concept album about childhood. The inherent whimsy of the Worldpeace DMT project suits these songs, which wring dry humour from lyrics about spiders, tigers and anthropomorphised guitars. Fincham and Miles sing in a self-consciously childish way that belies their taut musicality: a lush, almost Van Dyke Parks jauntiness on Munich Gyaru, for example, or a knack for bulletproof pop structure on the title track. The result is the kind of devastatingly contemporary record that even arch classicists couldn’t possibly turn up their noses at. Continue reading...

data.title: Weird Baile: Collected Rips 2004-2024 review – a hallucinatory trip to baile funk’s outer limits
data.description: (TraTraTrax) Two decades of work from producers JLZ, VHOOR, Mu540 and DJ RaMeMes strips the Brazilian genre to its essential parts until it chimes with grime and drill Originating in 1980s Brazil, baile funk began as a bass-heavy blend of syncopated folk rhythms and hip-hop-influenced sampling, and has since developed into regional styles ranging from the hyperpop freneticism of D.Silvestre to DJ K’s eerie and cacophonous bruxaria and the house-sampling sound of MC Lan. Coming together by sharing baile funk edits on SoundCloud, producers JLZ, VHOOR, Mu540 and DJ RaMeMes began releasing their own version in 2017 as Weird Baile. Now compiling two decades of their lo-fi productions as Collected Rips 2004-2024, Weird Baile establish their sound as a curious blend of Brazilian and British dancefloors. Sparse, harsh and artfully arranged, the Weird Baile signature strips baile funk down to its essentials: vocals, bass and rhythm. Opener Aquecimento Do Ih Caraca embodies this ethos with its industrial sub-bass, chopped-up shouted vocals and percussive beatboxing, producing two minutes of menacing intensity. The mood matches perfectly with the similarly abrasive energy of grime instrumentals, and on Grime Do Weird Baile the group mix the instantly recognisable vocalisations on Skepta and JME’s 2006 Rhythm & Gash Freestyle beat with clattering electronic percussion and Portuguese lyrics. This connection to the UK bass continuum continues with the skittering drill bass of PPRT and the cavernous, dubstep-influenced sounds of CaFaGesTeh, as well as in the ambient opening of Pique da Oakley, which calls back to dubstep producer Mala’s 2007 track Changes. data.title: Mendelssohn: Songs Without Words review – Chamayou makes each piece feel somehow familiar yet fresh
data.description: Bertrand Chamayou (Warner Classics) The pianist brings a singing quality and seeming effortlessness to the complete set of Songs Without Words Mendelssohn wrote 48 Songs Without Words for solo piano: eight sets of six, mostly under three minutes long, emerging over a 16-year period that spanned most of his short adult life. The handful that still regularly make their way on to recital programmes are only the tip of the iceberg; the complete set hasn’t been recorded as much as you might think, which makes this new release from Bertrand Chamayou still more welcome. These pieces belong to the world of Schubert Lieder, and Chamayou brings a singing quality to them from the off. The Duetto that rounds off the Op 38 set is beautifully done, the melodic lines alternating like a female and male voice, each lingering just slightly as the other voice takes over. Compared to other interpreters, Chamayou is often softer-edged, his playing a little smoother and more flowing, although there are exceptions: Op 62 No 6 – known as Spring Song, but originally titled Camberwell Green after the then-elegant London suburb where it was written – is given a perky, almost frothy touch in the accompaniment: spring bubbling under like frogspawn in a pond. data.title: Vermeer by Andrew Graham-Dixon audiobook review – a sharp and authoritative guide
data.description: The author offers intriguing insights into the way this Dutch artist worked, including fresh perspectives on The Girl With the Pearl Earring In the decades after the death of the Dutch artist Johannes Vermeer in 1675, few knew his name or work. He was so unknown that his paintings were sold with the forged signatures of more popular artists attached. All that changed in the mid-19th century, when his art was reassessed by French critics. Today Vermeer is one of the most admired painters in the world, although, says art historian Andrew Graham-Dixon, he has “proved stubbornly resistant to interpretation”. Vermeer: A Life Lost and Found, Graham-Dixon’s biography which was six years in the writing, endeavours to answer some unresolved questions, among them: what was Vermeer’s life like? Why did he paint the way he did? What was the intent behind his paintings, of which only 36 exist? Unlike the Dutch genre painters of his time, the Delft-born Vermeer painted solemn yet luminous works featuring women in domestic settings and engaged in activities such as reading, writing, playing music or pouring milk. His ability to render light, and its softening effect on rooms and people, was unparalleled. Continue reading...

data.title: From Mario to machine guns: how Ubisoft Paris made Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Tactics
data.description: The studio is swapping the Mushroom Kingdom’s vivid palette for the blood-soaked grit of military action series Where do you go after Mario? It’s a question the team at Ubisoft Paris found itself pondering three years ago after wrapping up work on the charming turn-based tactics adventure, Mario + Rabbids: Sparks of Hope , sequel to its unexpected crossover hit, Mario + Rabbids: Kingdom Battle. By melding a rather specialist genre with video gaming’s biggest household name, the developer introduced chin-stroking strategic play to a whole new audience. “ Having the opportunity to work with the Mario franchise was a privilege, and it’s still something I’m very proud of,” says level designer director, Julien Vial. “I still remember seeing the first prototype and being blown away by all the possibilities . ” Now, Ubisoft Paris has returned with a new project, but this time the studio is swapping the Mushroom Kingdom’s vivid palette for the blood-soaked grit of military action series Rainbow Six. Where Mario and Rabbids saw squishy creatures bounce harmlessly across levels as Mario encased foes in honey, Rainbow Six Tactics, a turn-based tactical spin-off from Rainbow Six Siege , sees balaclava-clad insurgents take shrapnel rounds to the chest. A seamless tonal shift, then. Continue reading...

data.title: Frieze review – you’ll see more avant garde wonders in the Bake Off tent
data.description: Regents Park, London This year’s art fair is a jumble sale of mediocre paintings for the super-rich, while its Masters sibling hawks dinosaur skulls and sleazy 19th-century nudes. Welcome to the art market as its most grotesque Naked people climb out of the earth and run around waving their arms and screaming, while someone with a bird’s head and wings plays the bagpipes. It’s my favourite artwork at this year’s Frieze but don’t go looking for this wildly imaginative outrage among the heaps of contemporary art at Frieze London. It’s a painting by a 16th-century follower of Hieronymus Bosch and is on view at Frieze Masters, the posher tent on the other side of Regent’s Park. I’m sorry to say I was bored rigid in Frieze London. Many people attend, I imagine, hoping to be informed and excited by the newest, coolest art, but you’ll see more genuinely avant garde wonders in the Bake Off tent. There are endless paintings, none of which are much good, interspersed with photographs which tend to be a little better. The first thing here that held me at all was a two-metre-tall, inkjet print by Wolfgang Tillmans called Paul, nude, golf ball in which the naked Paul has his elbows on the floor and his close-cropped head bowed between them in apparent despair, while the white ball beside him eerily mirrors the pale flesh of his bony back. But it’s not new – it dates from 1994. Continue reading...

data.title: Pope.L review – savage satire from Y-fronts-wearing trickster famed for gruelling ‘crawl’ across New York
data.description: Modern Art, London The late American took on liberal presumptions and the commercialism of Black culture, even dressing in white bunny ears and underpants Seven squares are pinned to the wall, each one painted in the high style of American minimalism: pure, austere variations on a theme. At the centre of each is printed the phrase “negro idea” followed by an apparently random number (51, 37, 666). What is Pope.L, the late, great trickster of contemporary American art, getting at? Perhaps it is a critique of how minimalism, with its ethos of art-for-art’s sake, excluded politics from art? Or a comment on how racial categories are as constructed (and as subject to fashion) as the theories underpinning contemporary art? Or is it a riff on how the edifice of western modernism is built on stolen ideas? Then again, maybe the deployment of an outmoded racial category is simply designed to discomfort the liberal pieties of those people likely to visit this art gallery just off Piccadilly. Continue reading...

data.title: Helen Goh’s recipe for baked oats with morello cherries and almond | The sweet spot
data.description: This moreish, flapjack-style oaty bake, flavoured with maple syrup and dotted with sour cherries, works as well for dessert as it does for breakfast I’ve been making versions of these baked oats ever since discovering Heidi Swanson’s recipe in Super Natural Every Day . This is my favourite store-cupboard version, for when stone fruit and berries have slipped out of season. Morello cherries are a dark, tart variety of sour cherry, with an intensity of flavour and bright acidity that stand up particularly well to baking. I love them here paired with almonds and coconut drinking milk (the light kind sold in cartons, not the rich tinned variety). The cherries I use are whole fruit in syrup, which I drain and dot over the oats – they remain distinct while becoming deliciously jammy as they bake. Almost any fruit compote or jam will work here, though, so choose your favourite. Continue reading...

The cherries I use are whole fruit in syrup, which I drain and dot over the oats – they remain distinct while becoming deliciously jammy as they bake. Almost any fruit compote or jam will work here, though, so choose your favourite. Continue reading...

data.title: Sedimentary rocks: why pét nat and cloudy wines are on the rise
data.description: There’s something refreshing about unfiltered or unfined wines. We filter through a selection … Centuries ago, Geoffrey Chaucer observed that “ther is no newe gyse that it nas old”. This truth – that there is nothing new under the sun – certainly applies to wine: every year, a well-documented or ancient viticultural practice is repackaged for a mainstream that greets it giddily as an innovation. Orange wine! Wine in kegs! Chilled reds! And, in 2026, cloudy wine, courtesy of Marks & Spencer’s peachy-opaque organic rosé, Trouble (a name that means “ cloudy ” in French. Trouble is the first cloudy still wine available in a British supermarket, a development that has seemed inevitable since pét nat – pétillant naturel – hit the big time; it’s an ancestral method of making sparkling wine that involves bottling before fermentation has finished. Typically, pét nats are not disgorged (that is, the dead yeast cells left over from fermentation are not removed), which is what gives them a cloudy appearance. They are also often fresh and tangy, so they suit warm weather, but it’s hard to imagine a better pairing for a pizza takeaway on an autumn evening, and without prosecco’s divisive sherbety notes, to boot. (That said, look out for rustic, cloudy col fondo – bottle fermented, undisgorged prosecco – a hazy, lively and bracing take on the nation’s most popular fizz.) M&S, ever quick on the uptake, has an own-label English rosé pét nat (currently out of stock), while Tesco sells a pét nat chardonnay from Argentina. Continue reading...

data.title: Gen Z wrestle with shame from ordering delivery food: ‘This economy is not for the weak’
data.description: As Americans use apps like DoorDash and Uber Eats more habitually, they confront the guilt of paying extra fees for convenience Tell us: what is your personal ‘recession indicator’? When it comes to food, Caroline Bauldree does not like to “deprive” herself of anything. She does not like to cook either, so that means a lot of food deliveries. “If I want sushi, I’m getting sushi,” said the 24-year-old nanny, who lives in Raleigh, North Carolina. “I’m definitely lazy in that regard.” Bauldree got into the habit of near-daily DoorDashing back in college. “I could order whatever food from whatever restaurant and it showed up at my door – that’s the dream,” she said. “But then I just feel like crap about myself because I’m like, ‘wow, I’m a lazy piece of shit.’ Nine times out of 10, I feel bad about myself.” Continue reading...

data.title: My autumn of comfort TV and comfort food
data.description: From batch-cooked dal and chicken barley to sticky toffee pudding, these are the cosy dishes that make October evenings at home feel special • Sign up here for our weekly food newsletter, Feast After a summer spent travelling here, there and everywhere, I am welcoming more time at home and bingeable telly with open arms. And, like a lot of the nation, I am obsessed with this season’s Celebrity Traitors . It is my achilles heel; so much so that, earlier this year, I politely declined an invite to a hot industry party because it clashed with the final, and there is no amount of free champagne or hobnobbing that would’ve got me off my sofa. The beauty of such shows is that they are on early enough to make an evening of it. Strictly has become our Saturday night family ritual, while my eldest will usually join us for Tuesday nights watching Bake Off . There are bowls of food, eaten by the spoonful, mugs of tea and endless biscuits. It’s a small, cosy ritual that makes the passing of summer feel a little less bleak. For ease, I try to live by the rule of one meal for everyone. On nights when we eat on the sofa, I like to make something in advance that the girls can eat after school and that we can return to later on. Nigella Lawson’s chicken barley , for instance, is a firm favourite and, importantly, if a little less glamorously, it reheats well. The same goes for Laura Goodman’s mac’n’cheese , a surefire hit and a fixture in our house. Continue reading...

data.title: They asked for 80 homes – she gave them 157! Council-housing miracle named Britain’s best new building
data.description: Rising from bluebell woodlands and framed by rolling hills, this cluster of pink and brown brick towers in Croydon is a bittersweet winner of the prestigious RIBA Stirling prize If Andy Burnham is looking for inspiration for his great “ council housebuilding comeback ”, he would do well to visit Croydon. There, nestled into a steeply sloping site, sheltered by a canopy of mature trees, stands a cluster of crystalline pink and brown brick towers, where generous flats look on to a landscape of allotments, playgrounds and to the rolling hills of south London beyond. Designed by Mary Duggan Architects, with Ruff Architects, it is a model of council-led housebuilding – so much so that it has also been named this year’s best building in the UK, confounding the bookies’ outsider odds. Only once before has the RIBA Stirling prize ever been awarded to a council housing project, when Goldsmith Street in Norwich scooped the gong in 2019, for its rows of low-energy brick terraces, designed by Mikhail Riches Architects and Cathy Hawley. This year’s winner, Lion Green Road in Coulsdon, is an entirely different animal, and it puts a welcome spotlight back on housing design at a time when the government plans to pump £39bn into the sector. It is also a bittersweet vindication of Croydon council’s erstwhile housebuilding company, Brick by Brick, a bold and sadly brief experiment by the previous Labour administration, which was halted in 2020 when the council went bankrupt, seeing numerous projects cancelled. Continue reading...

data.title: Trump should fear the BBC. Instead he’s picked a fight – and he seems to be losing | Emma Brockes
data.description: The president is used to bullying his media targets. The quagmire that is his libel actions shows the broadcaster is working to a different script For the greatest account of the BBC’s finest hour, one must turn to Penelope Fitzgerald’s novel, Human Voices, written in 1980 and set 40 years earlier, at the corporation’s Portland Place wartime HQ. Flanked by sandbags and infused with a smell of cooking “from the deep hold that suggested more strongly than ever a cruise on the Queen Mary”, the organisation that Fitzgerald describes is at once noble and deeply eccentric. “Broadcasting House stood headed on a fixed course south,” she writes. “With the best engineers in the world, and a crew varying between the intensely respectable and barely sane, it looked ready to scorn any disaster.” In other words, a formidable foe, one that in the spring of 1940, in the face of anticipated Nazi invasion, decided “without prompting, that truth was more important than consolation, and, in the long run, would be more effective”. I bring this up in respect to the gathering storm of Donald Trump versus the BBC, a fight triggered by the US president’s $10bn defamation lawsuit – $10bn! It’s a wonder he didn’t go for $10 gazillion – brought against the corporation at the end of last year in response to a poorly edited episode of Panorama. The BBC was at fault, editing together comments made by the US president at a rally on 6 January 2021 to give, as the corporation’s apology put it, “the mistaken impression that President Trump had made a direct call for violent action”. But it is fighting the lawsuit. Emma Brockes is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: Ukraine war briefing: Starlink access restored, says UK’s Streeting after Hegseth meeting
data.description: UK defence secretary says Pete Hegseth assured him satellite communications system back up and running in Ukraine. What we know on day 1,696 Ukraine’s access to Elon Musk’s Starlink had been restored, according to UK defence secretary Wes Streeting. Ukraine said Starlink services had been restricted on Wednesday, hampering the country’s attack and air-defence drone missions, and triggering a new rift between Washington and Kyiv. On Thursday, Streeting said his US counterpart, Pete Hegseth, had assured him in a face-to-face meeting that the vital satellite communications system was back up and running. He said it was unclear what had caused the disruption, but added: “This is not the first time we’ve seen a falling out between Washington and Kyiv.” The order to limit Starlink access came from inside the White House , according to a report by Reuters, citing two US officials and a western official briefed on the matter. The ⁠officials said leaders at the defence ⁠department received a message that the service for the Ukrainian military needed to be slowed. The officials, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, did not specify who in the White House made the decision or who was responsible for implementing the order. The Pentagon is the biggest customer of Starshield, which ⁠is the military-grade version of the Starlink service . Amid growing doubts about long-term US commitment to Ukraine, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy met Nato chief Mark Rutte in Brussels and held a string of bilateral meetings with European leaders before he was set to join an EU summit on Friday. French president Emmanuel Macron on Thursday said it was “crucial” that Ukraine receive “all the means necessary to protect itself” after meeting Zelenskyy. “I can reassure you, dear Ukrainian friends and President Zelenskyy: YOU ARE NOT ALONE,” Polish prime minister Donald Tusk posted online. Vladimir Putin has said that recent ⁠Ukrainian ​strikes on Russian oil refineries had not caused significant ⁠damage and vowed that Moscow would respond. “They ⁠hit here and there. Nothing ​particularly significant. Nevertheless ‌they are ‌carrying on,” the Russian president was quoted as saying by the Interfax news agency. His comments ‌came after a major Ukrainian drone attack ignited a fire at an oil refinery in Russia’s Ryazan region on Thursday morning, according ‌to the regional governor. It was the first confirmed ​Ukrainian attack on a Russian energy facility since US president Donald Trump abruptly declared an “energy ceasefire” that neither Russia nor Ukraine said they had agreed to. The US treasury department has extended a sanctions waiver on Russian oil company Lukoil for service stations outside Russia through April 2027. Thursday’s announcement allows Lukoil-branded stations in countries like the US to continue serving customers until 24 April next year. The extension comes a week after Trump said he had secured an agreement with Russia to supply diesel to American and global markets, with the US treasury issuing a temporary licence to enable flows. The latest licence, like an earlier one, does not allow the “transfer of funds to any person or account located in the Russian Federation”. Three people were killed and six others injured after the Kirovohrad region of central Ukraine came under a Russian drone attack lasting more than 10 hours , Ukraine’s emergency services said Thursday. Between midnight and Thursday morning, Russia launched more than 850 drones at Ukraine, Zelenskyy said on X. He added that the barrage came “precisely at a time when the speed of our defensive capabilities is being artificially restricted,” an apparent reference to the Starlink restrictions on drones. Russian aerial attacks hit 15 Ukrainian regions, he said. Continue reading...

data.title: Barbra Streisand’s $10 million gift helps women’s heart centre treat 1,700 patients annually
data.description: Barbra Streisand's generous donation of $10 million to Cedars-Sinai has paved the way for the creation of the Women’s Heart Center. This groundbreaking facility aims to delve into the disparities in cardiovascular health among women, addressing unique diagnostic and treatment challenges. Annually, over 1,700 women benefit from specialized cardiac care, emphasizing tailored medical approaches for heart disease, ultimately showcasing the critical need for research in women's health.

data.title: Trump: Nejsem fanda Zelenského, ukrajinské útoky na rafinerie jsou hanebné
data.description: Americký prezident Donald Trump prohlásil, že „není fanda“ ukrajinského prezidenta Volodymyra Zelenského. data.title: Poslanci chtějí elektronicky hlídat, že mladší 18 let nekupují alkohol online
data.description: Poslanci tří opozičních stran – hnutí STAN, lidovců a Pirátů – společně navrhují, aby u online prodeje alkoholu musel prodejce lépe hlídat, kdo ho kupuje. Prosazují, aby musel být vybaven počítačovým systémem, který elektronicky jednoznačně ověří věk, že kupujícímu není méně než 18 let. A věk bude pak muset ověřit i při předání.

data.title: Trump nás dohodou s Putinem podrazil, prohlásil Babiš
data.description: Český premiér Andrej Babiš se po včerejším jednání v Bruselu domnívá, že se lídrům nejspíš nepodaří dosáhnout dohody o budoucím víceletém rozpočtu EU do konce letošního roku. Stane se tak nejspíš až v únoru či v březnu, uvedl Babiš při příchodu na druhý den summitu. Babiš se vyjádřil také k současné situaci ohledně rusko-ukrajinského konfliktu. Uvedl, že americký prezident Donald Trump nás podrazil.

data.title: Opozice chce, ať Juchelka poví, proč kvůli poradkyni stát přijde o desítky milionů
data.description: Šéf opoziční ODS Martin Kupka navrhl, aby poslanci jednali o střetu zájmů Alexandry Semancové, bývalé poradkyně ministra práce a sociálních věcí Aleše Juchelky. Poslanci nyní řeší úpravy programu svého jednání.

data.title: Rusko oznámilo datum schůze se Slováky. Budou se řešit ruští sportovci i energie
data.description: Zástupci Ruska a Slovenska se sejdou v Moskvě na zasedání mezivládní komise 26. října. Za slovenskou stranu ji povede ministr zahraničí Juraj Blanár. S odvoláním na ruskou vládu to napsala státní agentura TASS. Půjde o první takové zasedání po pěti letech. Předmětem jednání údajně bude mimo jiné spolupráce v energetice. Slovenské opoziční strany plánovanou cestu kritizují.

data.title: Slováci našli v ohořelém autě tělo bez hlavy, ležela opodál. Stopa vede do Česka
data.description: Hasiči přivolaní k požáru osobního auta v lese na západě Slovenska po uhašení plamenů objevili ve vraku vozu Škoda Fabia s českou poznávací značkou tělo bez hlavy. data.title: Pane premiére, přiveďte k nám vodu z Baltu, radí objevitel pramenů Amazonky
data.description: Odsolit vodu z Baltského moře a přivést ji potrubím do Česka. I takovou možnost boje se suchem navrhuje hydrolog a geograf Bohumír Janský, profesor z Přírodovědecké fakulty Univerzity Karlovy, který se svým týmem objevil prameny Amazonky. V pořadu Rozstřel na iDNES.cz vysvětlil, proč potřebujeme další přehrady, jak omezit plýtvání pitnou vodou a proč by si lidé s vysokou spotřebou měli připlatit.

data.title: Tmavé vlasy, oči či ubytovna jako vodítko. Metodika zjišťování Romů pobouřila školy
data.description: Tmavé vlasy, oči nebo ubytovna jako vodítko. Učitele a vedení některých ostravských škol zarazilo šetření ministerstva školství, které zjišťuje počty romských žáků na základě odhadů podle vzhledu či kulturních zvyklostí. Zatímco podle kritiků i pedagogů metodika zavání stereotypy, ministerstvo i odborníci postup hájí – jde podle nich o jediný způsob, jak zmapovat segregaci a diskriminaci dětí, které okolí jako Romy vnímá bez ohledu na to, zda se k původu samy hlásí.

data.description: Voliči v pátek a v sobotu ve druhém kole voleb rozhodnou, kdo je bude za Přerovsko a Litovelsko zastupovat příštích šest let v Senátu. data.title: Kamion uvázlý v pražské Krči tam neměl co dělat, řidiči chybělo povolení
data.description: Uvázlý kamion v Praze ve Vídeňské ulici neměl podle magistrátu povolení k vjezdu do oblasti, kde je zákaz pro vozidla nad 12 tun. Chyběl mu také souhlas k nadměrné přepravě. Policie jako jednu z příčin uvádí nezajištěný náklad, nehodu stále vyšetřuje. Škody vyčíslila na několik desítek milionů korun.

data.title: Tým pro Jihlavu se dohodl se STAN, kritik Hošek zůstane řadovým zastupitelem
data.description: Povolební vyjednávání v Jihlavě dospělo ke klíčovému milníku. Vítězný Tým pro Jihlavu (sdružující ODS, KDU-ČSL a TOP 09) podepsal memorandum o spolupráci se Starosty a nezávislými (STAN). Tisková konference po středečním podpisu dohody ale ukázala, že uvnitř vítězného bloku nepanovala stoprocentní shoda a otevřeně se mluvilo o citlivých osobních vazbách.

data.title: Proč ANO zůstalo ve Zlíně mimo hru? Rozhodl nejen tlak ze sociálních sítí
data.description: Měl slušnou šanci obhájit post primátora. Jiří Korec sice ve volbách oproti roku 2022 ztratil deset procent, ale jeho ANO i tak těsně vyhrálo. Ještě před úplným sečtením všech hlasů na jeho volební štáb dorazili zástupci Zlína 21 a ODS. A s ANO se po nočním jednání shodli na rámcové spolupráci. Stačilo se dohodnout s lidovci a/nebo Piráty a Zlín by měl (staro)novou vládu.

data.title: Rusko znovu porušilo energetické příměří s Ukrajinou. Části Kyjeva jsou bez elektřiny
data.description: Část ukrajinské metropole se opět ocitla bez elektrického proudu. Rusko zasáhlo objekt kritické infrastruktury v Kyjevské oblasti a podle tamních úřadů tak znovu porušilo energetické příměří. Výpadek sítě okamžitě způsobil i pokles tlaku vody ve čtvrtích na pravém břehu Dněpru. Opravárenské čety čekají, až jim bezpečnostní situace dovolí vyrazit do terénu.

data.title: Senátní volby 2026: Hlasovací lístky pro druhé kolo vám domů nepřijdou. Kde je dostanete?
data.description: Na sadu hlasovacích lístků k nadcházejícímu druhému kolu voleb do Senátu budou voliči čekat marně. Do schránek vůbec nepřijdou. Voliči se k nim však bez problémů dostanou. Volby v pátek 16. a v sobotu 17. října 2026 proběhnou stejným způsobem, jako uplynulé první kolo. V každém z 22 volebních obvodů se bude vybírat vždy jen ze dvou kandidátů.

data.title: To prostě nejde. Kuba zuří kvůli koalici jeho hnutí s ANO v Mariánských Lázních
data.description: V Mariánských Lázních to vře. Zastupitel za Naše Česko Samuel Zabolotný údajně nerespektoval dohodu, kterou po volbách uzavřel se stranami Starostové a nezávislí, koalicí ODS a KDU-ČSL a Za lepší Mariánské Lázně. Naopak podpořil koalici tvořenou ANO a hnutím Změna pro Mariánské Lázně, což by současnému vedení umožnilo zůstat v Mariánských Lázních u kormidla a dál vést tamní radnici. To se však nelíbí zakladateli hnutí Naše Česko (NČ) Martinu Kubovi.

data.title: Kolik stála cesta k volbám? Pavel zveřejnil částku, odmítá ale zásah do soukromí
data.description: Prezident Petr Pavel zaplatil za cestu na dovolenou v Maroku 3 750 eur (91 tisíc korun) a za let k volbám a zpět 15 tisíc eur (365 tisíc korun) ze svých vlastních peněz. Prezidentská kancelář Pavlovu soukromou cestu neplatila ani neorganizovala. Do Česka se prezident vrátil běžnou linkou tento čtvrtek. Zveřejnil to dnes ve svém prohlášení.

data.title: Proces s Číňanem viněným ze špionáže pokračuje. Může padnout rozsudek
data.description: Čínský občan, který měl v Česku pod novinářským krytím sbírat informace, opět stane před soudem. Jang I-ming čelí obžalobě z neoprávněné činnosti pro cizí moc. data.title: Srážka autobusu s nákladním vlakem u Eurotunelu. Zraněných jsou dvě desítky
data.description: U vjezdu do Eurotunelu na francouzské straně se srazil autobus s nákladním vlakem. Zraněno bylo 19 lidí, z toho dva vážně. Nikdo ze zraněných není v ohrožení života, uvedly francouzské úřady. Provoz nákladních vlaků byl v obou směrech dočasně přerušen, osobních vlaků se událost nedotkla, informovala francouzská média.

data.title: USA omezily Ukrajině systém Starshield na přímý pokyn Bílého domu
data.description: Spojené státy v minulých dnech omezily Ukrajině využívání družicového systému Starshield na přímý pokyn Bílého domu. Ve čtvrtek se však podle nich jeho fungování zlepšilo.

data.title: Prix Bohemia Radio startuje v neděli, do Olomouce přiveze i program pro studenty
data.description: Český rozhlas v neděli 18. října zahájí už 42. ročník mezinárodního festivalu rozhlasové a audio tvorby Prix Bohemia Radio. Během pěti dnů se v Olomouci utká 37 finalistů z 167 přihlášených soutěžních děl o vítězství ve čtyřech kategoriích. Během doprovodného programu se budou moci příznivci rozhlasu potkat se známými, a nejen rozhlasovými osobnostmi, stát se publikem natáčení živých přenosů pořadů, diskuzí, koncertů či divadelních představení.

data.title: DP World ILT20 exposure proves a catalyst as Kuwait’s stars shine on the international stage
data.description: Kuwait's cricket stars are thriving on the international stage, thanks in part to their experiences in the DP World ILT20, which has significantly prepared them for competition. Bilal Tahir and Mohamed Shafeeq highlighted how the league improved their skills and understanding of the game, contributing to Kuwait topping the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2028 Sub-Regional Asia A Qualifier. As several players prepare for the next ILT20 season, they express excitement about further developing their talents alongside world-class cricketers.

data.title: Fijian conjoined twins separated at Riyadh hospital after nearly 13-hour operation
data.description: Fijian conjoined twins Jasepeli and Desicia were successfully separated in a nearly 13-hour operation at King Abdullah Specialized Children’s Hospital in Riyadh, involving a team of 34 medical professionals. The surgery marks the first separation of conjoined twins from Fiji and the 74th operation within Saudi Arabia's Conjoined Twins Program, which has been running for over 35 years.

data.title: À ROME, L’HISTOIRE GAGNE TOUJOURS
data.description:
Pendant 83 minutes, la Roma a fait le match parfait. Elle a été plus juste, plus forte, plus belle. Plus inspirée. Soulé virevoltait comme une étincelle dans la nuit, Malen dévorait l'espace à pleines foulées, Dybala puis Mora dessinaient des diagonales d'orfèvre. Chaque sortie de balle était une respiration, chaque pressing une morsure. En face, le Real errait. Amorphe, sans liant, sans tranchant, presque indigne de son blason. 
 Et c'est logiquement la Roma qui a ouvert le score à la 20e minute, par Marten de Roon, récompensée de son audace et de son pressing haut. 
 Le Real, acculé, n'a dû son salut qu'à un miracle de Mbappé cinq minutes plus tard, à la 25e, un ballon contré devenu lob improbable pour égaliser contre le cours du jeu, et à un Courtois des grands soirs qui, à lui seul, colmatait les brèches. 
 La Roma a mené 3-1 pendant 83 minutes, le Real n'a eu besoin que de 7 pour lui voler son histoire. 3-4 au final.
 Mercredi 14 octobre 2026, 22h54 à l'Olimpico. Une soirée que Rome n'est pas prête d'oublier.

data.title: Cinq grands matchs de la semaine : aperçu et pronostics de MELBET
data.description: © MelBet La semaine prochaine nous réserve plusieurs affiches particulièrement intéressantes. Dans cette sélection, MELBET vous présente cinq matchs à ne surtout pas manquer. Real Madrid vs Séville, LaLiga, 18 octobre Après huit journées, le Real Madrid occupe la quatrième place avec 18 points. Séville est cinquième avec 14 unités. Les Madrilènes comptent déjà six points de retard sur Barcelone et n’ont certainement pas envie d’en laisser trois de plus à domicile. D’autant que Séville ne s’est plus imposé au Santiago Bernabéu en LaLiga depuis décembre 2008. Presque 18 ans ! De quoi terminer l’école et entrer à l’université. Gagner à Madrid semble décidément plus compliqué. La saison dernière, le Real avait remporté les deux confrontations : 2-0 à domicile et 1-0 à l’extérieur. Seul bémol : Vinícius a été expulsé lors de la dernière journée face à Villarreal après avoir tiré Nathan Saliba par les cheveux. Son absence pourrait même, qui sait, profiter à l’équipe. Notre pronostic : victoire du Real Madrid à 1,25. Leeds vs Manchester United, Premier League, 18 octobre Après six journées, Leeds occupe la septième place avec 9 points. Manchester United est treizième avec 6 unités. United n’a remporté qu’un seul match. En revanche, l’équipe n’a pas manqué d’alimenter les mèmes. Lors de la dernière journée, les Red Devils menaient face à Tottenham tout en évoluant en supériorité numérique. Mais Solanke a égalisé à la deuxième minute du temps additionnel : 1-1. Conserver l’avantage face à dix joueurs s’est visiblement révélé trop compliqué. Leeds sait aussi contrarier son rival. La saison dernière, le club a pris quatre points face à Manchester United : 1-1 à domicile, puis victoire 2-1 à Old Trafford. Ce succès en avril était d’ailleurs le premier de Leeds en championnat dans ce stade depuis 45 ans. Cette saison en Premier League, Leeds n’a encore jamais perdu à domicile. Manchester United, de son côté, n’a toujours pas gagné à l’extérieur. Notre pronostic : match nul à 3,6. Liverpool vs Villarreal, Ligue des champions, 20 octobre Les quatre précédentes confrontations européennes entre ces deux équipes ont toutes eu lieu en demi-finales : en Ligue Europa 2015/16 et en Ligue des champions 2021/22. Liverpool en a remporté trois, Villarreal une. Score cumulé : 8-3 en faveur des Anglais. À Anfield, les Espagnols n’ont encore jamais marqué : défaite 3-0 en 2016, puis 2-0 en 2022. Les souvenirs de leurs déplacements à Liverpool ne sont donc pas franchement réjouissants. Cette fois, les deux équipes vont s’affronter pour la première fois en phase de ligue. Pour espérer prendre sa revanche, Villarreal devra déjà commencer par trouver le chemin des filets à Anfield. Pour l’instant, nous faisons davantage confiance aux locaux. Notre pronostic : victoire de Liverpool à 1.515. PSG vs Barcelone, Ligue des champions, 20 octobre Le PSG et Barcelone se sont affrontés à 16 reprises en compétitions européennes officielles. Le bilan est parfaitement équilibré : six victoires chacun et quatre matchs nuls. Même le nombre de buts est identique : 29-29. En 2017, le Barça avait gagné 6-1 après s’être incliné 4-0 à Paris. À l’époque, les Catalans étaient entraînés par Luis Enrique. Aujourd’hui, il dirige le PSG. Les Parisiens sont les champions d’Europe en titre. La saison dernière en Ligue des champions, ils avaient battu Barcelone 2-1 malgré une infirmerie bien remplie ! Cette affiche a aussi une dimension personnelle. Ferran Torres a quitté Barcelone pour rejoindre le PSG cet été. Il y a un an, il avait marqué contre les Parisiens. Cette fois, il pourrait trouver le chemin des filets face à son ancien club. C’est l’un des grands matchs de la saison. Impossible de le manquer. Sinon, comment continuer à se dire fan de football ? Notre pronostic : match nul à 4.28. Bayern vs Arsenal, Ligue des champions, 21 octobre Le Bayern a remporté huit de ses 15 confrontations avec Arsenal en Ligue des champions. Différence de buts : 31-18. Entre 2015 et 2017, les Munichois se sont même imposés trois fois de suite sur le score de 5-1. Même pour infliger une correction, on peut varier les plaisirs. Lors de leurs cinq duels à élimination directe, le Bayern s’est toujours qualifié. Le plus récent remonte à 2024. Arsenal a donc suffisamment de raisons de ne pas apprécier les déplacements à Munich. Mais la saison dernière, les Londoniens se sont imposés 3-1 à domicile. Preuve que les lourdes défaites du passé ne sont plus forcément une fatalité. Harry Kane constitue une autre raison de suivre cette affiche. À huit ans, il a passé une année à l’académie d’Arsenal. Les Gunners ont aujourd’hui de quoi le regretter. L’ancien pensionnaire de leur centre de formation tentera une nouvelle fois de marquer face au club londonien. Notre pronostic : victoire du Bayern à 2.15. Du grand football au programme pendant plusieurs soirées. Tu as déjà choisi tes vainqueurs ? Teste ton flair foot et parie sur tes favoris avec MELBET ! Cet article Cinq grands matchs de la semaine : aperçu et pronostics de MELBET est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Yaoundé : le Cameroon International Tech Summit place les droits de l’enfant au cœur du numérique
data.description: © DR Le Cameroun accueille du 15 au 17 octobre 2026 le Cameroon International Tech Summit, sous le thème "Advancing child rights through digitalization". Trois jours de panels, d'expositions et de rencontres entre gouvernement, PNUD, GIZ, UNICEF, Ambassade des États-Unis et acteurs tech, pour promouvoir une transformation numérique inclusive au service des enfants et des jeunes. C'est le grand rendez-vous tech de l'année. La cérémonie d'ouverture du Cameroon International Tech Summit a réuni le 15 octobre 2026 à Yaoundé des représentants du gouvernement, des partenaires techniques et financiers et des acteurs clés de l'écosystème technologique. Pendant trois jours, le sommet propose un espace d'échanges et de découverte à travers des panels thématiques, des stands d'exposition et des présentations d'entreprises technologiques et de startups, mettant en lumière les innovations et les opportunités offertes par le numérique au Cameroun. Au-delà de la vitrine technologique, le sommet affiche une orientation politique forte : faire du numérique un levier pour les droits. À travers sa participation, l'UNICEF réaffirme son engagement en faveur d'une transformation numérique inclusive, qui place les enfants et les jeunes, notamment les plus vulnérables et les plus souvent exclus, au cœur de l'innovation. Dans son allocution, Juliette Haenni, Représentante adjointe de l'UNICEF au Cameroun, a souligné l'importance de développer des solutions numériques durables, intégrées aux systèmes nationaux et adaptées aux besoins des enfants. Elle a également mis en avant le rôle des partenariats entre les pouvoirs publics et le secteur privé pour favoriser des solutions accessibles, sécurisées et capables d'améliorer concrètement la vie des enfants. Un message en phase avec les priorités du gouvernement camerounais, qui fait de la digitalisation un axe de sa Stratégie Nationale de Développement, mais aussi un rappel : l'innovation ne vaut que si elle est inclusive, protégée et ancrée dans les systèmes publics d'éducation, de santé et de protection sociale. Cet article Yaoundé : le Cameroon International Tech Summit place les droits de l’enfant au cœur du numérique est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: IA générative en CEMAC : le Gabon largement en tête, 15% de la population concernée
data.description: © DR Au 1er trimestre 2026, 15,0% de la population gabonaise utilise l'IA générative, contre 8,7% pour le Cameroun, la Centrafrique, le Tchad et le Congo, selon un classement compilé par l'Agence Ecofin sur la base de données Microsoft. Le Gabon se hisse au 4e rang africain, loin devant ses voisins de la CEMAC classés entre la 32e et la 35e place. La Guinée équatoriale n'est pas classée. Le fossé est net au sein de la Communauté Économique et Monétaire de l'Afrique Centrale. D'après les données Microsoft relayées par l'Agence Ecofin, le Gabon s'impose comme le champion sous-régional de l'adoption de l'IA générative au 1er trimestre 2026. Avec 15,0% de sa population utilisatrice, le pays occupe le 1er rang CEMAC et le 4e rang à l'échelle africaine. Une performance qui le place dans le top 5 continental, signe d'une diffusion rapide des outils d'IA générative auprès du grand public et des entreprises. Derrière, le peloton est groupé à un niveau deux fois moins élevé. Le Cameroun est 2e en CEMAC avec 8,7% de la population, mais seulement 32e en Afrique. Il est suivi de près par la Centrafrique (3e CEMAC, 33e Afrique, 8,7%), le Tchad (4e CEMAC, 34e Afrique, 8,7%) et le Congo (5e CEMAC, 35e Afrique, 8,7%). data.title: Douala : la Communauté urbaine lance une campagne de contrôle des moto-taxis et tricycles
data.description: © journalducameroun.com L’opération qui associe le contrôle des engins à deux et à trois roues et la sensibilisation des conducteurs et usagers débute ce jeudi 15 octobre et vise à renforcer la sécurité routière dans la ville de Douala. Les moto-taxis et tricycles de la ville de Douala sont soumis dès ce jeudi à une campagne de sensibilisation et de contrôle organisée par la Communauté urbaine de Douala. L’opération concerne les conducteurs de motos et de tricycles. Et vise en même temps le renforcement de la sécurité routière et l’amélioration de la mobilité urbaine. Les équipes déployées dans certains carrefours de la capitale économique insisteront sur l’obligation pour les conducteurs de respecter les feux tricolores ainsi que les règles de circulation routière, l’obligation du port du casque de protection, l’interdiction du port de babouches ou des chaussures inadaptées pendant la conduite. D’autres points sur lesquels les équipes vont mettre l’accent sont le port des chasubles réglementaires permettant de les identifier, l’équipement des motos et tricycles en rétroviseurs et en clignotants en bon état de fonctionnement. Sur le terrain, les équipes de sensibilisation et de contrôle sont mixtes. Elles se composent des éléments de la police municipale, des ambassadeurs du bon ordre urbain et des représentants des organisations de motos-taxis. Elles ciblent les conducteurs et les usagers, les ramènent au respect des prescriptions relatives à la préservation de la sécurité dans les rues de la ville de Douala, plus grande ville du Cameroun. Estimée entre 3,7 et 4,4 millions d’habitants en 2026 selon des sources, la population de Douala se déplace en grande majorité grâce aux moto-taxis. Une étude diagnostique du secteur des moto-taxis à Douala réalisée en 2025 a permis de comprendre que ledit secteur représente 61% des déplacements dans la ville. Il assure cette mission aux côtés des taxis et des bus. Ce secteur rassemble à lui seul environ 100 000 conducteurs dont 90% évoluent dans le secteur informel, toujours d’après les résultats de cette étude validés en mars 2025. Au regard de ces données, l’importance de l’opération de sensibilisation et de contrôle des motos et tricycles n’est plus à démontrer. Cet article Douala : la Communauté urbaine lance une campagne de contrôle des moto-taxis et tricycles est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: BDEAC : première réussite sur les marchés internationaux avec 222 millions de dollars levés
data.description: © DR Le 13 octobre 2026, la Banque de développement des États de l'Afrique centrale (BDEAC) a réussi sa première émission obligataire internationale de 222 millions de dollars. Une opération à coupon de 7,88% en euros après couverture de change, à échéance octobre 2029, qui augmente de près de 15% la surface bilantielle de la Banque et marque une étape majeure de son Plan Stratégique 2023-2027 « AZOBE ». C'est une première qui change de dimension. Depuis Brazzaville, le 14 octobre 2026, la BDEAC a annoncé le succès de son entrée sur les marchés internationaux de capitaux. « Cette opération qui consacre l'accès à une nouvelle source de financement pour la BDEAC, témoigne de la confiance croissante des investisseurs internationaux dans ses fondamentaux financiers », a déclaré son Président, Dieudonné Evou Mekou. Il y voit aussi la reconnaissance du soutien à la transformation et à la modernisation de la Banque engagée ces dernières années. L'opération a été marquée par la participation de l'Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) en qualité d'Investisseur d'Ancrage Stratégique, aux côtés d'autres investisseurs de premier plan. Les ressources mobilisées permettront d'accélérer les décaissements en faveur du développement économique, de l'intégration régionale et des projets structurants - infrastructures, agriculture, agro-industrie, industrie - dans les six États membres de la CEMAC. Cette primo-émission s'est accompagnée d'engagements en matière de transparence : organisation de conférences semestrielles avec les investisseurs et publication semestrielle d'une présentation résumant soutien des actionnaires, performance du portefeuille, financement et liquidité. Elle fait suite à l'obtention d'une notation internationale « Ba3 » perspective stable, attribuée par Moody's en novembre 2025 et confirmée en septembre 2026. Elle constitue une première étape vers un accès durable aux marchés internationaux. Le même jour, la BDEAC a signé un accord de prêt de 30 millions d'euros avec la Banque Arabe pour le Développement Économique en Afrique (BADEA). Objectif final affiché : faire de la BDEAC « le socle du développement durable des économies de l'Afrique Centrale » et atteindre à terme une notation Investment Grade. Cet article BDEAC : première réussite sur les marchés internationaux avec 222 millions de dollars levés est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : le Minresi lance Reach pour booster les financements de la recherche
data.description: © DR Le secrétaire général du Minresi, Pr Rebecca Madeleine Ebelle Etame, a lancé le 14 octobre 2026 à Yaoundé l'atelier fondateur du programme REACH - Research Empowerment And Capacity Hub, destiné à renforcer l'accès des instituts de recherche camerounais aux financements compétitifs nationaux et internationaux. C'est un réseau pour muscler la recherche camerounaise. Porté par le Ministère de la Recherche Scientifique et de l'Innovation, avec l'appui scientifique de l'IRD et le soutien du Service de coopération et d'action culturelle de l'Ambassade de France au Cameroun, REACH vise à renforcer durablement les compétences en montage de projets. Dans son allocution d'ouverture en salle des conférences du MINRESI, en présence des représentantes de l'Ambassade de France et d'experts de l'IRD, le Pr Ebelle Etame a souligné la nécessité d'accompagner les jeunes chercheurs recrutés ces dernières années sous le leadership du Dr Madeleine Tchuinte. « Il répond à un besoin vital pour nos huit instituts de recherche », a-t-elle déclaré. Le dispositif mobilise dix-neuf correspondants issus des instituts, du futur Centre de Biogéosciences de l'Environnement et du Ministère. Retenus après présélection puis évaluation par un comité mixte, ils auront pour mission de diffuser les compétences acquises. « Vous êtes les représentants de vos instituts dans le programme REACH mais aussi bientôt les ambassadeurs du dispositif », leur a-t-elle rappelé. L'atelier se tient en deux séquences, du 14 au 16 puis du 19 au 21 octobre 2026. Au menu : ingénierie de projet, réponse aux appels, construction budgétaire et exigences des bailleurs. Le programme, étalé sur 36 mois, prévoit 16 ateliers de dissémination pour toucher environ 240 chercheurs, du coaching personnalisé, des webinaires et une plateforme numérique. Cet article Cameroun : le Minresi lance Reach pour booster les financements de la recherche est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: MRC : retrait de Pierre Emmanuel Binyam, une leçon de 2026 (Me Hyppolite Meli)
data.description: © DR L’avocat défenseur des militants du MRC et ancien président de l’Assemblée générale du Barreau du Cameroun réagit après le retrait de la candidature de M. Binyam à la tête du MRC. Il exprime son respect et son admiration pour Pierre Emmanuel Binyam qui se détache pour bien s’élever. La course pour la présidence du Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun reste celle de Tiriane Balbine Noah. Pierre Emmanuel Binyam se retire. Non sans dénoncer des irrégularités sur le processus électoral, en particulier sur le fichier électoral. Suite à son action, il bénéficie de la sympathie et de l’admiration de Me Hyppolite Meli Tiakouang. L’homme de droit fervent défenseur des militants du MRC voit en Emmanuel Binyam l’un de ceux qui feront l’avenir du Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun. Un parti qui traverse une période difficile de son histoire après la performance réalisée à la présidentielle de 2018 (classée 2è). Et suite aux manifestations de contestation des résultats dudit scrutin, au boycott des élections législatives et municipales du 09 février 2020 ainsi que des régionales de décembre de la même année. Pour Me Meli, le fait que le candidat se retire après avoir décidé d’entrer en compétition, de poursuivre, de quitter avant échéance après toutes les logistiques mobilisées alors que certains sondages donnent des chiffres de victoire en sa faveur suscite respect. Car « ils sont rares ceux laissent tomber à ce moment », fait-il remarquer. Pour avoir pris une décision pareille en 2012 au Barreau, il laisse lire derrière les mots que Pierre Emmanuel Binyam ne regrettera pas d’avoir pris cette décision. Tous ceux qui suivent un leader ne sont pas toujours des amis ni des soutiens sincères, explique-t-il. Leur proximité avec le leader peut s’expliquer par des intérêts incompatibles avec les objectifs d’intérêt communs poursuivis ou défendus par le leadership. Il voit en cet acte de retrait une leçon de 2026 en référence à la leçon de 2008 lorsque Hilary Clinton se retirait de la compétition au profit de Barack Obama. La leçon en question peut servir au MRC comme elle peut être utile à l’opposition en général. Lors de la présidentielle de 2025, alors que les pronostics étaient favorables à une opposition coalisée, des leaders ont manqué de se tenir main dans la main pour faire front commun. Cet article MRC : retrait de Pierre Emmanuel Binyam, une leçon de 2026 (Me Hyppolite Meli) est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : les listes électorales provisoires de 2026 sont disponibles (Elecam)
data.description: © DR Elections Cameroon annonce ce jeudi la publication des listes électorales provisoires dans les 360 communes du pays. Six semaines après la clôture de la campagne annuelle de révision des listes électorales, Elections Cameroon annonce la publication des listes électorales provisoires. Dans un court message illustré publié ce 15 octobre sur sa page Facebook, l’organe chargé de l’organisation de la gestion et de la supervision des élections au Cameroun déclare la disponibilité des listes électorales provisoires sur l’ensemble du territoire national. L’institution précise en outre que ces listes sont consultables au niveau de ses antennes communales. Elles sont disponibles cinq jours avant la limite fixée par le Code électoral en son article 78(2). Leur disponibilité est l’occasion donnée aux partis politiques, aux électeurs de vérifier leur inscription et pour demander des corrections éventuelles. En cas de problème constaté, les concernés peuvent saisir la commission de révision de listes électorales ou la commission départementale de supervision pour signaler des irrégularités constatées. Les opérations de rectification qui s’en suivent se terminent au plus tard le 10 novembre. Le fichier révisé quant à lui parvient à la direction générale le 10 décembre en provenance des délégations régionales d’Elecam. Les opérations vont prendre fin avec la publication de la liste électorale nationale le 30 décembre par le directeur général des élections. Pour rappel, au terme de la révision des listes électorales le 31 août 2026, le directeur général des élections, Erik Essousse, a communiqué les statistiques le 1 er septembre. 252 830 nouveaux électeurs ont été enregistrés dont 150 954 hommes, 101 876 femmes, 169 225 jeunes et 176 personnes vivant avec un handicap. Le fichier électoral national non toiletté compte au 31 août 8 238 778 électeurs. La liste électorale nationale attendue le 30 décembre prochain devra contenir le fichier toiletté et consolidé. Elle servira de base pour les élections législatives et municipales prévues en février 2027. Cet article Cameroun : les listes électorales provisoires de 2026 sont disponibles (Elecam) est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

Pour rappel, au terme de la révision des listes électorales le 31 août 2026, le directeur général des élections, Erik Essousse, a communiqué les statistiques le 1 er septembre. 252 830 nouveaux électeurs ont été enregistrés dont 150 954 hommes, 101 876 femmes, 169 225 jeunes et 176 personnes vivant avec un handicap. Le fichier électoral national non toiletté compte au 31 août 8 238 778 électeurs. La liste électorale nationale attendue le 30 décembre prochain devra contenir le fichier toiletté et consolidé. Elle servira de base pour les élections législatives et municipales prévues en février 2027. Cet article Cameroun : les listes électorales provisoires de 2026 sont disponibles (Elecam) est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Ebola: plus de 9 000 cas et 4 410 décès en RDC, un deuxième cas confirmé au Kenya
data.description: Cinq mois après sa déclaration officielle, l’épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola de souche Bundibugyo reste active et meurtrière en République démocratique du Congo (RDC).
