data.title: Gobierno espera acceder a la Cuenta del Milenio en 2027 y obtener hasta $1,000 millones
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- El Gobierno de Honduras espera ser elegible por la Cuenta del Milenio en 2027 y acceder a un compacto entre 800 y 1,000 millones de dólares en donación de Estados Unidos. Así lo reveló este día el secretario de Finanzas, Emilio Hernández Hércules, durante una presentación de los logros de los primeros ocho meses de gestión del presidente Nasry Asfura. Agregó que el Gobierno tiene en marcha una estrategia para calificar a la Cuenta del Milenio, iniciativa que fue elegible en 2006, o sea hace 20 años, y se accedió a 205 millones de dólares. Para 2026, la aspiración del Gobierno es calificar al Programa Umbral . "Hay una genuina oportunidad para acceder a la Cuenta del Milenio", subrayó el funcionario. Añadió que esos fondos se destinarían para sectores como energía, puerto y conectividad. En cuanto al tema de corrupción que Honduras ha sido reprobada en los últimos años, Hernández Hércules dijo que hay una serie de medidas que están en práctica. Destacó que este año se han otorgado más recursos al Tribunal Superior de Cuentas (TSC), al Ministerio Público (MP), a la Procuraduría General de la República (PGR) y al Instituto de Acceso a la Información Pública (IAIP), que son instituciones que luchan contra la corrupción. De acuerdo con el secretario de Finanzas, en este Gobierno hay más control en el tema de corrupción y en transparencia. Anunció que la próxima revisión de la Cuenta del Milenio evaluará otros indicadores propuestos por el Gobierno de Honduras.

data.title: Viceministro de Salud llama a médicos a reincorporarse a sus labores tras semanas en paro
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- El viceministro de Salud, Eduardo Midence, hace un llamado al gremio médico a que se incorporen a sus labores, luego de 39 días de paro de labores exigiendo el pago de salarios atrasados En comparecencia en Casa Presidencial, el viceministro dijo: "hemos estado esta última semana en diferentes contextos y en la especial con el Colegio Médico". "3,092 niños y niñas no han recibido las atenciones pediátricas donde los médicos han dicho que no debido a que están atendiendo las directrices del Colegio Médico", destacó Midence. Destacó que hasta el día de hoy el 97% de los médicos están pagados, por lo que  "les hacemos el llamado a que se incorporen a sus labores". "Es nuestro deber ciudadano hacer el llamado para que se incorporen a sus labores", reiteró el viceministro de Salud. En cuanto a las Unidades Médicas, manifestó que siguen desplazándose a las comunidades para atender a la población. "La junta directiva del Colegio Médico ha hecho un llamado a detener las actividades, por lo que estas Unidades Médicas son una alternativa en materia de salud", destacó el funcionario. Recordó que el presidente Nasry Asfura viajará a Estados Unidos para conocer equipos tecnológicos de última generación para detectar el cáncer y busca fortalecer las capacidades para el diagnóstico oportuno de esta enfermedad. El Colegio Médico de Honduras (CMH) exige el pago de salarios atrasados a sus agremiados, luego de varios meses de atención a pacientes sin recibir su cuota mensual correspondiente. Aunque, la Secretaría de Salud sostiene que han avanzado en la regularización de los salarios pendientes y buscan una salida negociada con el gremio médico, entre 200 y 250 profesionales están pendientes de recibir sus pagos. El subsecretario de Salud, José Miguel Castillo, y autoridades del gobierno afirman que se ha cumplido con el 95% al 96% de las obligaciones salariales de los galenos.

data.title: Manuel Zelaya regresa a Honduras luego de recibir el alta médica en México
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Honduras.- El expresidente hondureño y coordinador general del partido Libertad y Refundación (Libre), Manuel Zelaya Rosales , regresó este jueves 15 de octubre al país luego de permanecer en México , donde recibía atención médica especializada por una afección cardíaca. El exmandatario arribó al aeropuerto internacional Ramón Villeda Morales, en San Pedro Sula, después de que su médico autorizara el alta, al considerar que podía continuar con el tratamiento desde su domicilio en Honduras . “Ayer me dieron de alta, siempre bajo supervisión de los médicos. Yo estoy enfermo, no vengo curado, vengo a un tratamiento, solo que no es tan agresivo, es leve, entonces puedo hacerlo en país, dura casi dos años el tratamiento”, explicó Zelaya. La salud del también coordinador general de Libre había generado preocupación en distintos sectores políticos y entre sus seguidores, luego de que a inicios de septiembre fuera sometido a una intervención quirúrgica de emergencia en Honduras debido a una acumulación de líquido alrededor del corazón. Posteriormente, el 7 de septiembre, Zelaya viajó a México para continuar con estudios médicos especializados y determinar las causas de la afección que había presentado. Durante su permanencia en territorio mexicano, dirigentes y allegados al exmandatario compartieron información sobre su evolución, aunque los detalles específicos de su diagnóstico y tratamiento se mantuvieron limitados. El pasado 11 de octubre, la subcoordinadora de Libre, Rixi Moncada, informó que Zelaya se encontraba estable mientras continuaba con su tratamiento médico, luego de visitarlo en México. Además de confirmar su regreso, Zelaya anunció que volverá a participar en las actividades del partido Libertad y Refundación (Libre), aunque deberá continuar bajo vigilancia médica. “En lo que compete, voy a retomar mis actividades en el Partido Libre, pero también está Rixi Moncada que ha cumplido muy bien su papel como subcoordinadora”, expresó al ser consultado sobre su participación en la organización política. Finalmente, se refirió a la versión que se divulgó sobre su posible muerte cuando viajó al país azteca. “Aquí estoy para seguir esta lucha”, dijo al tiempo que reprochó a los que celebraron su presunto deceso.

data.title: Dictan auto de formal procesamiento contra Melvin Cevallos por coacción y amenaza electoral
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- La justicia hondureña dictó un auto de formal procesamiento contra Melvin Cevallos Umanzor , cabecilla de los colectivos del partido Libertad y Refundación ( Libre ), por los delitos de coacción y amenaza electoral, en perjuicio de la Constitución de la República. La resolución fue dictada por un juez de Letras Penal tras celebrar la audiencia inicial, en un caso relacionado con presuntas acciones que obstaculizaron el proceso electoral de 2025. Según el requerimiento fiscal, Cevallos Umanzor encabezó y dirigió movilizaciones que impidieron el normal desarrollo del proceso de recepción de ofertas para garantizar el funcionamiento del sistema de Transmisión de Resultados Electorales Preliminares (TREP), de cara a las elecciones generales de noviembre de ese año. La Fiscalía atribuye al imputado acciones que habrían afectado un procedimiento clave para la organización electoral. Por estos hechos, deberá continuar enfrentando el proceso judicial, aunque el juez le otorgó medidas sustitutivas a la prisión preventiva. La audiencia preliminar quedó programada para el lunes 26 de octubre de 2026, a las 9:30 de la mañana, fecha en la que el caso avanzará a la siguiente etapa procesal.

data.title: Siete plazas de Tegucigalpa se iluminan de rosa durante octubre
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- Siete plazas de Tegucigalpa y Comayagüela permanecerán iluminadas de rosa durante el resto de octubre como parte de las actividades de sensibilización sobre el cáncer de mama. La iniciativa de la Alcaldía Municipal del Distrito Central (AMDC) busca recordar a la población la importancia de la detección temprana y de acudir a los servicios de salud para realizarse los controles médicos correspondientes. Los espacios intervenidos están ubicados en distintos puntos de la capital, varios de ellos cerca de centros comerciales, instituciones educativas y centros de salud. Las plazas que lucen la iluminación rosa son la ubicada frente a Mall Premier; Centro América, frente a Plaza Miraflores; Simón Bolívar, frente al Hospital San Felipe; República Dominicana, frente a la Escuela Americana. También la que esta frente a la Basílica de Suyapa; Las Banderas, frente a la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de Honduras (UNAH), e Isis Obed Murillo, al costado sur del aeropuerto Toncontín. Denovan Galicia, gerente de Microempresas de la municipalidad, explicó que la iluminación busca transmitir un mensaje de solidaridad con las personas que enfrentan la enfermedad y sus familias. Durante octubre, conocido como el Mes Rosa, distintas iniciativas buscan informar sobre el cáncer de mama, promover la detección temprana y recordar la importancia de recibir atención médica oportuna. La detección temprana puede facilitar el diagnóstico y el acceso al tratamiento. Por ello, los especialistas recomiendan que las mujeres consulten con personal de salud sobre los controles adecuados según su edad, antecedentes familiares y factores de riesgo. Además de prestar atención a posibles cambios en las mamas, es importante buscar evaluación médica si se detectan bultos, alteraciones en la piel, hundimientos o secreciones inusuales. La iluminación de las plazas permanecerá durante lo que resta de octubre, en una campaña que busca mantener visible el mensaje de prevención y acompañamiento a quienes viven con esta enfermedad. La Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS) y reportes de organizaciones como Funhocam señalan que en Honduras se diagnostican cerca de 1,200 nuevos casos de cáncer de mama al año.

data.title: Defensa de Mario Zelaya pidió su traslado a los Cobras y Fuerzas Especiales dio el visto bueno
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. Sin que se conociera públicamente, la defensa de Mario Roberto Zelaya Rojas , exdirector del Instituto Hondureño de Seguridad Social ( IHSS ), gestionó su traslado al Comando de Operaciones Especiales (Cobras). Un documento obtenido en exclusiva por EL HERALDO Plus revela que la Dirección Nacional de Fuerzas Especiales (DNFE) respondió que cuenta con el espacio y las condiciones para recibirlo. Se trata del Oficio DGPN-(DNFE)-No. 855-2026, fechado el 9 de septiembre de 2026, el cual responde a una solicitud que el abogado Francisco Pascua Cantarero, defensor privado de Zelaya Rojas, presentó el martes 8 de septiembre. En ella pedía el visto bueno y un informe de condiciones para el traslado del privado de libertad. En su respuesta, la DNFE asegura que sus instalaciones disponen de seguridad, custodia, alojamiento, atención médica y control de visitas familiares y de su defensor privado, para que Zelaya Rojas “pueda ser trasladado en su condición de privado de libertad a estas instalaciones”. El oficio añade que se tomarán las medidas necesarias para salvaguardar su integridad física y el respeto a sus derechos humanos, “garantizando la tutela efectiva”. Lo firma el comisionado de policía Carlos Vladimir Pacheco , director nacional de Fuerzas Especiales. Hasta ahora, no se ha confirmado si el traslado se ejecutó ni si cuenta con la autorización del juez de ejecución, requisito para cambiar de centro penitenciario a una persona condenada. La solicitud tampoco detalla las razones para trasladar al reo a una instalación policial, pues no se reportan agresiones en su contra ni situaciones de riesgo que justifiquen la medida EL HERALDO Plus consultó al abogado defensor de Zelaya Rojas, quien mencionó que el motivo de la solicitud es "por la seguridad del privado, ya que corre riesgo y actualmente no se le están respetando sus derechos". Asimismo, este medio buscó la versión del Instituto Nacional Penitenciario (INP), así como la de la defensa de David Castillo, sin obtener respuesta al cierre de esta nota. Ese mismo 9 de septiembre, la DNFE emitió el Oficio DGPN-(DNFE)-No. 856-2026, también en poder de EL HERALDO Plus. Está dirigido al abogado Jorge Alberto Juárez Rodríguez, defensor privado de José Ramón Bertetty Osorio , exgerente administrativo y financiero del IHSS y coimputado de Zelaya en la mayoría de los procesos por el desfalco. Según una fuente de entero crédito de este medio, la intención es que Bertetty también sea trasladado a esas instalaciones, al igual que David Castillo Mejía, exgerente de la empresa Desarrollos Energéticos S.A. (DESA), condenado a 22 años y seis meses de prisión como coautor del asesinato de la ambientalista Berta Cáceres. La fuente con conocimiento del sistema penitenciario, que pidió el anonimato por temor a represalias, explicó a EL HERALDO Plus que detrás de estas solicitudes estaría el interés de acceder a mejores condiciones de reclusión que las de un centro penal común, como el de la cárcel de Támara. “No quieren requisas, quieren privilegios, tener comunicación, teléfono celular, quieren estar VIP, que los visiten todos los días, porque en Támara podrán tener sus privilegios, pero no se comparan. Ellos buscan estar en la jugada nuevamente porque su partido político está en el poder”, afirmó la fuente. Según su versión, el objetivo sería ocupar las mismas instalaciones donde han estado recluidos políticos de alto perfil. Entre ellos está el expresidente Juan Orlando Hernández, quien permaneció en la sede de Fuerzas Especiales tras su captura en 2022 y antes de su extradición a Estados Unidos. Zelaya dirigió el IHSS entre 2010 y 2014, período en el que se cometió el mayor saqueo a la institución. Tras el escándalo se dio a la fuga y fue capturado en la frontera con Nicaragua luego de pasar más de 200 días prófugo. Su captura ocurrió el 9 de septiembre de 2014, exactamente doce años antes de la fecha del oficio de Fuerzas Especiales y desde entonces ha acumulado sentencias en distintas líneas del caso. Para 2021 ya sumaba 101 años de cárcel. Ese año, la justicia le impuso otros 30 años por un contrato con la Constructora JC Maradiaga, a través del cual se lavaron casi 50 millones de lempiras. El 16 de junio de 2026, la Sala IV del Tribunal de Sentencia en Materia de Criminalidad Organizada, Medio Ambiente y Corrupción condenó a Zelaya y Bertetty a nueve años y siete meses de prisión en el caso de los “14 contratos” . Ese caso se refiere al desvío de L158 millones mediante 14 contratos de obras públicas, civiles, eléctricas y mecánicas suscritos de forma irregular. De acuerdo con el Ministerio Público, con esa sentencia ambos suman 10 condenas y más de 100 años de prisión.

data.translatedDescription: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. Sin que se conociera públicamente, la defensa de Mario Roberto Zelaya Rojas , exdirector del Instituto Hondureño de Seguridad Social ( IHSS ), gestionó su traslado al Comando de Operaciones Especiales (Cobras). Un documento obtenido en exclusiva por EL HERALDO Plus revela que la Dirección Nacional de Fuerzas Especiales (DNFE) respondió que cuenta con el espacio y las condiciones para recibirlo. Se trata del Oficio DGPN-(DNFE)-No. 855-2026, fechado el 9 de septiembre de 2026, el cual responde a una solicitud que el abogado Francisco Pascua Cantarero, defensor privado de Zelaya Rojas, presentó el martes 8 de septiembre. En ella pedía el visto bueno y un informe de condiciones para el traslado del privado de libertad. En su respuesta, la DNFE asegura que sus instalaciones disponen de seguridad, custodia, alojamiento, atención médica y control de visitas familiares y de su defensor privado, para que Zelaya Rojas “pueda ser trasladado en su condición de privado de libertad a estas instalaciones”. El oficio añade que se tomarán las medidas necesarias para salvaguardar su integridad física y el respeto a sus derechos humanos, “garantizando la tutela efectiva”. Lo firma el comisionado de policía Carlos Vladimir Pacheco , director nacional de Fuerzas Especiales. Hasta ahora, no se ha confirmado si el traslado se ejecutó ni si cuenta con la autorización del juez de ejecución, requisito para cambiar de centro penitenciario a una persona condenada. La solicitud tampoco detalla las razones para trasladar al reo a una instalación policial, pues no se reportan agresiones en su contra ni situaciones de riesgo que justifiquen la medida EL HERALDO Plus consultó al abogado defensor de Zelaya Rojas, quien mencionó que el motivo de la solicitud es "por la seguridad del privado, ya que corre riesgo y actualmente no se le están respetando sus derechos". Asimismo, este medio buscó la versión del Instituto Nacional Penitenciario (INP), así como la de la defensa de David Castillo, sin obtener respuesta al cierre de esta nota. Ese mismo 9 de septiembre, la DNFE emitió el Oficio DGPN-(DNFE)-No. 856-2026, también en poder de EL HERALDO Plus. Está dirigido al abogado Jorge Alberto Juárez Rodríguez, defensor privado de José Ramón Bertetty Osorio , exgerente administrativo y financiero del IHSS y coimputado de Zelaya en la mayoría de los procesos por el desfalco. Según una fuente de entero crédito de este medio, la intención es que Bertetty también sea trasladado a esas instalaciones, al igual que David Castillo Mejía, exgerente de la empresa Desarrollos Energéticos S.A. (DESA), condenado a 22 años y seis meses de prisión como coautor del asesinato de la ambientalista Berta Cáceres. La fuente con conocimiento del sistema penitenciario, que pidió el anonimato por temor a represalias, explicó a EL HERALDO Plus que detrás de estas solicitudes estaría el interés de acceder a mejores condiciones de reclusión que las de un centro penal común, como el de la cárcel de Támara. “No quieren requisas, quieren privilegios, tener comunicación, teléfono celular, quieren estar VIP, que los visiten todos los días, porque en Támara podrán tener sus privilegios, pero no se comparan. Ellos buscan estar en la jugada nuevamente porque su partido político está en el poder”, afirmó la fuente. Según su versión, el objetivo sería ocupar las mismas instalaciones donde han estado recluidos políticos de alto perfil. Entre ellos está el expresidente Juan Orlando Hernández, quien permaneció en la sede de Fuerzas Especiales tras su captura en 2022 y antes de su extradición a Estados Unidos. Zelaya dirigió el IHSS entre 2010 y 2014, período en el que se cometió el mayor saqueo a la institución. Tras el escándalo se dio a la fuga y fue capturado en la frontera con Nicaragua luego de pasar más de 200 días prófugo. Su captura ocurrió el 9 de septiembre de 2014, exactamente doce años antes de la fecha del oficio de Fuerzas Especiales y desde entonces ha acumulado sentencias en distintas líneas del caso. Para 2021 ya sumaba 101 años de cárcel. Ese año, la justicia le impuso otros 30 años por un contrato con la Constructora JC Maradiaga, a través del cual se lavaron casi 50 millones de lempiras. El 16 de junio de 2026, la Sala IV del Tribunal de Sentencia en Materia de Criminalidad Organizada, Medio Ambiente y Corrupción condenó a Zelaya y Bertetty a nueve años y siete meses de prisión en el caso de los “14 contratos” . Ese caso se refiere al desvío de L158 millones mediante 14 contratos de obras públicas, civiles, eléctricas y mecánicas suscritos de forma irregular. De acuerdo con el Ministerio Público, con esa sentencia ambos suman 10 condenas y más de 100 años de prisión.

data.title: Investigan muerte de dos hombres encontrados en un megaparque de Gracias, Lempira
data.description: Lempira, Honduras.- Dos hombres fueron encontrados sin vida en un megaparque del municipio de Gracias , departamento de Lempira , en el occidente de Honduras, en un hecho que permanece bajo investigación y cuyas circunstancias deberán ser esclarecidas por las autoridades. El hallazgo tuvo lugar muy cerca del bulevar Marco Tulio Rodríguez, en el casco urbano de este municipio occidental, donde los cuerpos quedaron encunetados y completamente ensangrentado. En la escena del crimen, las autoridades localizaron varios litros de guaro y de acuerdo con los reportes preliminares, ambas personas se encontraban ingiriendo bebidas alcohólicas antes de desatarse una riña. Hasta el momento, la información disponible no permite establecer con certeza la identidad de las víctimas ni la edad de los fallecidos. Por ahora, las autoridades trabajan con dos posibles líneas de investigación para esclarecer el crimen. Una de ellas plantea que los dos hombres pudieron atacarse mutuamente durante una discusión ocurrida bajo los efectos del alcohol, mientras que la otra posibilidad contempla la intervención de una tercera persona en el hecho. Ante lo ocurrido, equipos de la Dirección Policial de Investigaciones (DPI) llegaron al sitio para desarrollar las diligencias correspondientes y recolectar evidencias que contribuyan a determinar cómo sucedieron los hechos. Durante las labores investigativas, una mujer llegó al lugar con la intención de reconocer a uno de los fallecidos, aunque aparentemente no consiguió confirmar su identidad y hasta ahora se desconoce qué vínculo podría tener con alguno de los dos hombres. Por su parte, agentes de la Policía Nacional permanecen resguardando la escena mientras esperan la llegada del personal de Medicina Forense, encargado de efectuar el levantamiento legal de ambos cuerpos, en un caso que mantiene consternados a los habitantes de Gracias, Lempira.

data.title: Reforma sobre fondos incautados genera incertidumbre entre inversionistas de Koriun
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- Los inversionistas de Koriun se mantienen en alerta ante una nueva reforma presentada en el Congreso Nacional , debido a las posibles implicaciones que tendría sobre los fondos incautados por el Ministerio Público en el caso relacionado con esta empresa. La iniciativa legislativa plantea que los recursos incautados por la Fiscalía puedan ser utilizados para combatir la criminalidad , una medida que genera incertidumbre entre las personas que esperan recuperar el dinero vinculado a Koriun . Dicho escenario abre interrogantes sobre el destino de los fondos mientras avanza el proceso judicial y las condiciones legales que determinarían su utilización, especialmente si se emite una resolución favorable para el principal señalado en el caso. Uno de los aspectos relevantes es la posibilidad de que el exgerente de Koriun, Iván Velásquez , obtenga una sentencia absolutoria. De acuerdo con los datos proporcionados, si esto ocurre, el Estado estaría obligado a devolver los más de 353 millones de lempiras incautados. Esta posibilidad coloca el destino de los recursos en el centro de la atención, debido a que su eventual utilización para combatir la criminalidad podría generar obligaciones de restitución si una resolución judicial determina que corresponde devolverlos. Sin embargo, para establecer con precisión los alcances de esta situación, es necesario conocer el contenido de la reforma, las condiciones para disponer de los bienes incautados y las disposiciones legales que regularían una eventual devolución. El caso Koriun Inversiones se originó a partir de un informe de la Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera (UIF) de la Comisión Nacional de Bancos y Seguros (CNBS), que alertó sobre captación irregular de dinero por parte de esta empresa. Posteriormente, inspecciones realizadas en enero de 2025 revelaron la falta de documentación legal y financiera que acreditara el uso y destino de los recursos. Las investigaciones establecieron que Koriun Inversiones ofrecía a sus clientes una rentabilidad semanal del 5% (equivalente al 20% mensual), asegurando que recuperarían su inversión en cinco meses. Para atraer a más personas, emplearon una intensa campaña en redes sociales, principalmente en TikTok. En 2024, la empresa reportó ingresos por más de 86.9 millones de lempiras , provenientes de unos 35,000 inversionistas , sin embargo, no contaba con autorización de la CNBS ni estaba inscrita en el Registro de Actividades No Profesionales Designadas (APNFD). Koriun Inversiones operaba en al menos siete departamentos y, según las investigaciones, se encontraba en proceso de evadir responsabilidades e incluso podría haber intentado fugarse del país.

data.title: Dan último adiós a Yamileth, la niña que murió de cáncer en SPS:  "Ya me le habían dado el alta"
data.description: La Ceiba.- Entre lágrimas, dolor y consternación, familiares dieron el último adiós a la niña Yamileth Gutiérrez Carias de 5 años de edad, cuyo trágico deceso conmovió al país tras fallecer en los brazos de su madre en la terminal de buses de San Pedro Sula. El desgarrador hecho ocurrió la tarde de ayer miércoles, poco después de que a la menor le dieran el alta médica en el hospital Mario Catarino Rivas, donde recibía atención debido al cáncer que padecía. La familia, originaria de la zona de La Mosquitia, se encontraba en la terminal de transportes alistándose para emprender el viaje de regreso a su hogar. La madre de la niña, Lesia Carias, relató entre sollozos el difícil momento que atravesaron:"Es difícil lo que estamos pasando. Mi niña tenía cáncer desde hace cuatro meses que se lo diagnosticaron. En el hospital ya me habían dado el alta y me habían dejado cita para el próximo mes", expresó. Con profundo dolor, Lesia quien recordó los últimos instantes con su hija antes de su partida: "Mi niña me dijo que le diera comida, una yuca que miró, pero no se la pude comprar. Luego miré que no se movía y murió cuando la tenía chineada", apuntó la joven de 20 años de edad quien perdió a su única hija. Debido a que la familia es de escasos recursos económicos y no contaba con vivienda en la zona, los restos mortales de la pequeña Yamileth fueron velados en la colonia Olas del Mar, en La Ceiba, en la residencia de unos familiares de la menor. Esta mañana, el féretro fue trasladado hacia su última morada en el cementerio San Isidro de esta ciudad. El traslado contó con el respaldo directo de la alcaldía municipal de La Ceiba. Al respecto, Dilcia Ortiz, jefa de Desarrollo Comunitario de la comuna ceibeña, manifestó el compromiso de la institución ante este lamentable caso: "Estamos aquí porque este caso nos ha conmovido. Es lamentable lo que le ha ocurrido a esta familia y como municipalidad estamos colaborando", afirmó la funcionaria, quien además mencionó que el alcalde Bader Dip colaboró con los pasajes para que la madre de la menor regrese a La Mosquitia.

data.title: Nasry Asfura asistirá al Foro Económico de América Latina y el Caribe en Panamá en 2027
data.description: Ciudad de Panamá, Panamá.- El presidente de Honduras, Nasry Asfura , asistirá al Foro Económico de América Latina y el Caribe 2027, que tendrá lugar en la capital panameña el 27 y 28 de enero, organizado por el Gobierno y el Banco de Desarrollo de América Latina y el Caribe ( CAF ), informó el Ministerio de Exteriores de Panamá . La Cancillería panameña hizo este anuncio en un comunicado con motivo de la visita esta semana al país de la ministra de Exteriores hondureña, Mireya Agüero, que confirmó la participación de Asfura en el Foro de CAF en un encuentro con su homólogo de Panamá, Javier Martínez-Acha. El Foro reunirá a presidentes y jefes de Estado, líderes empresariales, organismos multilaterales, inversionistas, académicos, emprendedores y tomadores de decisión para impulsar el diálogo sobre el presente y el futuro de la región, según CAF. La visita de Agüero da continuidad a la agenda bilateral entre Panamá y Honduras, orientada al fortalecimiento de las relaciones diplomáticas y la cooperación entre ambos países, de acuerdo con la nota de la cancillería panameña. La canciller hondureña extendió por su parte una invitación al presidente panameño, José Raúl Mulino, para celebrar en 2027 en Honduras la conmemoración de los 120 años de relaciones diplomáticas entre las dos naciones. La visita de Agüero se produce tras el encuentro sostenido el pasado junio entre Mulino y Asfura, con motivo de la gira oficial a Panamá, en la que ambos acordaron fortalecer la cooperación bilateral y avanzar en los procesos del Sistema de la Integración Centroamericana (SICA).

data.title: Accidente de microbús deja varias personas heridas cerca del puente El Carrizal
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- En horas de la mañana de este jueves-15 de octubre- se registró un fatal accidente de tránsito tipo volcamiento que dejó varias personas heridas, entre ellas algunas de gravedad, en el bulevar Fuerzas Armadas, a cercanías del puente de la colonia El Carrizal. El hecho ocurrió a eso de las 6:20 de la mañana, cuando, según las declaraciones de algunos de los pasajeros, el bus habría intentado rebasar a otra unidad, provocando que este se volcara. En la escena se observa la unidad de transporte totalmente deshecha en la parte del vidrio, mientras en sus alrededores varios pasajeros se muestran visiblemente afectados. Una de las víctimas relató que "el bus venía lleno, él (conductor) quiso rebasarle al vehículo y no sé si maniobró mal el vehículo, pero el bus dio tres vueltas". Explicó que "gracias a Dios no hay muertos, pero quien resultó más herido fue el cobrador, él traía la mano afuera de la unidad y quedó deshecha". Agregó: "Una joven que se llevaron resultó afectada de la clavícula y otra de ellas resultó afectada en el área de la espalda". En otro de los extremos se muestra a víctimas llorando del dolor en el suelo, mientras se espera la ayuda de más ambulancias para ser trasladadas a un centro asistencial. De manera preliminar se informó que tanto el conductor como el cobrador, presuntamente ambos familiares, ya habrían sido trasladados al Hospital Escuela, pues fueron los más afectados en el incidente. Las autoridades de la Dirección Nacional de Vialidad y Transporte (DNVT) deberán determinar las circunstancias en las que ocurrió el accidente y establecer las responsabilidades correspondientes.

data.title: Eesti ja Soome vahele rajatakse uus merekaabel: põhjauuringud algavad juba järgmisel nädalal

data.title: Drivers' diligence tested in 'white cane' campaign in Latvia

data.title: Romania’s quantum computing hub in Iași adds Classiq software to IBM hardware
data.description: Classiq, a leading company in quantum computing software, and Romania’s FreeYa Mind Campus announced the signing of a strategic commercial agreement to develop quantum application creation, education, and adoption capabilities for companies and public institutions at the campus's Quantum AI center in Iași. Under the agreement cited by Economedia , FreeYa Mind Campus will provide access to Classiq's enterprise-grade quantum software platform, both on campus and throughout the Romanian ecosystem. The platform brings together Classiq's agentic AI interfaces, the high-level Qmod modeling language, circuit synthesis, and hardware-aware execution, helping researchers and corporate teams design optimized quantum applications faster. “Our partnership with Classiq will connect the quantum hardware available on campus and through the cloud with a leading application development and education environment that can serve universities, companies, and public institutions. This will help Romania develop sustainable quantum skills and contribute to Europe's broader technological objectives,” said Cristian Berariu, founder and CEO of FreeYa Mind Campus. The center was developed to provide on-site access to quantum hardware, including an IBM Quantum System Two . With this deal, the center is set to add Classiq's software, expertise, and training programs to further develop and expand quantum innovation and industrial applications. The initiative will build on the FreeYa Mind Campus network, which comprises companies, research institutions, public sector organizations, and academic partners, including more than 12 partner universities. The center will be open to government organizations and participants in programs funded by the European Union. Classiq will also contribute to expanding the center's training programs, from introductory quantum computing courses to high-level modeling and advanced algorithm design. Furthermore, in collaboration with the campus team, Classiq will connect quantum innovation to practical industrial applications. The campus will provide university curricula, specialist training, introductory programs for companies, advanced application development, and resources for Classiq certification. To support customer relations, project delivery, and application deployment, Classiq will establish its regional headquarters in Romania at FreeYa Mind Campus. “Europe's quantum ambitions depend on combining high-performance software with advanced hardware. Building on the success of FreeYa Mind Campus, we are bringing these components together, with Classiq providing the scalable software foundation that will enable universities, companies, and public institutions to develop quantum applications. This partnership accelerates ecosystem development and creates a clear path from business and research challenges to executable quantum solutions,” said Regev Yativ, CRO of Classiq. The agreement with the Iasi campus is part of Classiq's expanding work with organizations developing large-scale quantum hardware and software centers, application hubs, and local technology infrastructure. It follows Classiq's partnership with TEA TEK to create a quantum computing hub in Naples and its collaboration with QAI to launch a local Quantum-as-a-Service offering in South Korea, a first of its kind. The initiative enables the campus to support its own hardware strategy while introducing a model for developing quantum skills. The hardware provides the computing infrastructure, while Classiq's software component enables researchers, experts from various fields, and developers to learn, create, optimize, and execute applications. Named a “Next Big Thing in Tech” by Fast Company, Classiq is backed by leading global investors and works with quantum cloud service providers, hyperscalers, and quantum hardware companies.

data.title: Romania’s Central Depository targeted in cyberattack
data.description: The Central Depository, the entity through which all transactions on the Bucharest Stock Exchange (BVB) are carried out and which manages all data on transactions and contracts, was the target of a cyberattack on Friday, October 16. The attack impacted the Online Services for Investors application, according to the official press release. This application, which is auxiliary to the Central Depository system, is used to create user accounts for investors (Romanian individuals) interested in accessing the online services provided by the Central Depository. The incident was identified on the day it occurred, and the necessary investigation and remediation measures were taken immediately. System monitoring has been intensified, and operations are proceeding under normal conditions, according to the same source. “The incident did not affect the Central Depository’s critical services and functions related to settlement and registry operations, which are being carried out under normal conditions. In particular, financial instrument holdings and information regarding settled transactions were not accessed, modified, and/or altered,” the Central Depository added. At this time, no user data has been affected, and no information has been lost, because the IT system benefits from a highly efficient backup system, according to Economica . “At this time, the Application is temporarily unavailable. Based on the information available to us so far, personal data belonging to our users were viewed as a result of the cyberattack, namely data used in the user registration/account creation process: first and last name, address, personal numerical identification code, identity card series and number, email address, telephone number, and IBAN code. These data have not been modified and/or altered,” the Central Depository stated. The institution also said that it has already hired a team of specialists and notified the National Directorate for Cyber Security (DNSC) about the cyberattack. The Central Depository's message also includes the steps investors and other people using the application should follow. “Although your password for accessing the Application was not accessed during the cyberattack, if you use the same passwords for multiple online services, we recommend changing them and using separate passwords. Also, enable two-factor authentication, if available. We apologize for the concern and any inconvenience caused by this incident.”

data.title: Romanian-Austrian business platform Romania Connect launches in Bucharest
data.description: Romania Connect, a business platform for companies, entrepreneurs, and institutional partners from Romania and Austria, has launched in Bucharest. The move follows its initial launch in Vienna on March 23. The independent, apolitical association is financed through membership fees, its representatives said. It plans to facilitate partnerships through business events, structured networking, specialist referrals, mentoring, and market information. “We want to build a long-term, truly active business community between the two countries, which is currently missing, even though the conditions are there: we have a strong economic relationship, Austria is one of the biggest investors in Romania, and the Romanian community is the second largest foreign community in Austria,” said Romania Connect president Radu Stoica. “The interest is very high, but it's not organized, and our first goal is to become the framework where this interest turns into business decisions.” The platform primarily targets established, profitable Romanian companies with mature products but limited international operations. It identified IT and artificial intelligence, industry, energy, construction, and creative sectors as areas with potential in Austria. “Austria is a relationship-driven market, not a transaction-driven one,” Stoica said. “We are already receiving very diverse requests, from IT companies that see Vienna as a gateway to an entire region to manufacturers looking for distribution in the DACH area.” The platform also seeks to assist Austrian companies looking for suppliers, business partners, or investment opportunities in Romania, particularly in energy and real estate. Members define their industry, the type of partner they need, and their main objective for the following 12 months. Romania Connect then arranges individual introductions and sector-specific meetings based on those goals, according to its representatives. Austria can also provide Romanian businesses with access to Germany and Switzerland and serve as a regional hub for Central and Eastern Europe, the organization said. Romania Connect’s institutional partners include the Romanian Embassy in Austria, the Austrian Business Agency, WKO Advantage Austria, and the Moldovan Embassy in Austria.

Austria can also provide Romanian businesses with access to Germany and Switzerland and serve as a regional hub for Central and Eastern Europe, the organization said. Romania Connect’s institutional partners include the Romanian Embassy in Austria, the Austrian Business Agency, WKO Advantage Austria, and the Moldovan Embassy in Austria.

data.title: Romania’s BMF GRUP acquires ENGIE Building Solutions
data.description: BMF GRUP, a local entrepreneurial group founded in 2011, announced that it acquired ENGIE Building Solutions from ENGIE Servicii, a company owned by ENGIE Romania. The transaction was completed on October 15 following approval from the Competition Council, while its financial terms were not disclosed. ENGIE Building Solutions provides integrated technical management and energy services for industrial and commercial properties and office buildings. Its activities include technical maintenance and energy management, as well as engineering, procurement, and construction projects. The company’s portfolio covers photovoltaic installations, battery energy storage systems, building management systems, and projects designed to reduce energy use and carbon emissions. “Through this integration, we are strengthening our teams and expanding our range of facility management, energy efficiency, and decarbonization services,” said Gabriel Tomescu, co-founder and CEO of BMF GRUP. “We will use this expertise to coordinate our services more effectively and help clients manage their operating costs efficiently.” BMF GRUP said the acquisition would allow it to provide property management, maintenance, cleaning, and security alongside the design and implementation of building modernization projects. “The integration of the two organizations brings together our team’s expertise, strengthened by the many EPC projects we have delivered over the years, with BMF GRUP’s integrated offering and operational capabilities,” said Adina Susanu, director of ENGIE Building Solutions. Before the acquisition, BMF GRUP employed more than 5,000 people and managed over 15 million sqm of properties. The company expects its turnover to exceed EUR 120 million in 2026, with more than 93% generated through private-sector contracts. BMF GRUP was founded in Romania in 2011 and has been expanding in partnership with private equity firm SARMIS Capital since 2023. “This acquisition marks a decisive step forward in the consolidation strategy we committed to together with BMF GRUP from the outset of our partnership,” said Cezar Scarlat, managing partner and founder of SARMIS Capital. ENGIE Building Solutions has operated on the Romanian market since 2001. Its acquisition forms part of ENGIE’s strategic portfolio refocusing, while the energy group continues its other activities in Romania.

data.title: More Romanians have searched for jobs this year
data.description: The change compared with 2025 reflects the economic conditions of the past year, with 2026 marked by greater caution in the labour market over plans to expand teams. In terms of applications, the first nine months of the year saw the highest level in the past decade. A total of 10.4 million applications were registered in the first three quarters, 27% more than in the same period last year. “Candidates showed particular interest in jobs in retail, financial and banking services, call centres/BPO, the food industry, tourism, and IT and telecoms. Many of these sectors mainly offer entry-level positions, which explains why most applications came from candidates with between zero and two years of experience,” said Roxana Drăghici, head of sales, eJobs. Applications increased across all age groups this year. Candidates aged 25-35 remained the most active, accounting for 4.1 million applications, while those aged 18-24 also represented a significant share, with 2.8 million applications. Year-on-year increases were also recorded among candidates aged 36-45 and those over 45, who submitted 2.1 million and 1.2 million applications, respectively. “The increase in applications alongside a slight moderation in the number of new jobs shows that competition among candidates is intensifying. This year, we have already reached an average of 65 applications per job, with the figure exceeding 90 in sectors such as retail and IT and telecoms,” Roxana Drăghici concluded.

data.title: Romanian Liberals yet to confirm limited support for PM-designate Luca Niculescu
data.description: PNL will remain in opposition and support the government’s policies that are in line with its own strategy, party officials explained, as reported by G4media.ro . PNL president Ilie Bolojan announced that the party could vote for the government despite the presence of PSD ministers, in a bid to end the political crisis. In a post on his Facebook page on Thursday, Bolojan explained why the PNL might decide to support the Niculescu-led government. “The PNL will make a final decision at the end of this week,” the interim prime minister said. Bolojan recalled that the situation was becoming more complicated by the day with the government operating without full powers. “After five months of political crisis, with a government without full powers, the situation is getting more complicated every day. [...]  The PNL will make a final decision at the end of this week. For now, the parliamentary groups have recommended that we vote for the government on the basis of an agreement that we could sign with the designated prime minister. The agreement precisely outlines the limits of specific support, strictly for budgetary objectives, the principles of transparency, good governance and parliamentary democracy, and remains valid until spring 2027. We also reserve the possibility of voting for a motion of censure if these principles are violated,” Bolojan said. The PNL leader stressed that this would not mean restoring the former governing coalition and that the party would remain in opposition. “Therefore, we are not rebuilding the coalition, and we will not under any circumstances give unconditional support for the investiture. The vote will not be one of confidence. The vote will be for an exit from a long crisis that Romania can no longer afford. The responsibility for the team with which he will govern belongs exclusively to the technocratic prime minister appointed by the president of Romania. And that is normal: he has the duty to form a cabinet and secure an investiture majority."

data.title: Romania prolongs 25% cut in diesel excise duty
data.description: “This measure continues the intervention applied in the previous period, in a context marked by pressures on the fuel market. The mechanism is calibrated according to the evolution of international quotations and pump prices, with the aim of limiting their effects on the population and the economy,” the ministry said in a statement. The 25% reduction amounts to RON 701.07 per 1,000 litres, or RON 829.69 per tonne. Accordingly, the effective excise duty on standard diesel sold on the domestic market will remain at RON 2,103.22 per 1,000 litres, or RON 2,489.05 per tonne, over October 16-31. According to the ministry, the assessment for the October 16-31 period showed that Platts diesel quotations (VPM) had increased by 47.78%, while the average pump price of standard diesel (VM) had risen by 35.60%. Based on these indicators and the mechanism established by law, the 25% excise duty reduction will remain in force for October 16-31, 2026.

data.title: Markets’ sentiment improves after political agreement reached in Romania
data.description: Banks also submitted bids totalling five times the target amount for a 36-month bond issue tapped by the Treasury on October 15. The moves came as the main centrist political parties moved towards a political agreement that would pave the way for a minority government, five months after a successful no-confidence motion brought down the previous cabinet. Yields on 10-year Romanian government bonds have also declined to 7.1-7.2%, after spiking to 7.75% on September 30, when Parliament rejected the second prime ministerial nomination. However, the weighted-average yield on the 36-month bonds sold by the Treasury rose to 6.81%, from 6.54% in mid-September, when the same issue was last tapped.

data.title: Romania's Nuclearelectrica slashes 2026 profit target by 43% assuming it resumes operations on November 1
data.description: Thus, SNN estimated a reduction of 18.4% (over RON 991 million) in revenues from sold production, compared to the approved budget, caused by the unplanned shutdowns of the two reactors during 2026, which determined a decrease of over 25% (2,337 GWh) in the production forecast for the current year, from 9,080 to 6,743 GWh, Profit.ro reported. Compared to the current budget, SNN estimated a decrease of almost RON 1 billion in gross profit, from RON 2.4 billion to RON 1.404 billion, and of almost RON 900 million in net profit, from RON 2.064 billion to RON 1.177 billion. The company's market capitalisation contracted by 19% over the past six months, to under RON 18 billion. On an annual basis, it however maintains an advance of nearly 25%.

data.title: Romania’s current account deficit widens by 5% y/y in January-August, but deficit-to-GDP ratio eases
data.description: However, the current account deficit-to-GDP ratio declined to 5.1% over the period, based on the latest annual GDP data available, from 5.2% in the same period last year. Foreign direct investment inflows contracted to EUR 2.1 billion over the period, from EUR 5.7 billion in the same period last year. On the positive side, equity investments amounted to EUR 2.2 billion, partly offset by net repayments of intra-group loans. Romania’s gross external debt rose by EUR 7.4 billion in January-August to EUR 238 billion. The stock of intra-group loans increased by EUR 1 billion to EUR 54 billion, while the debt of deposit-taking corporations rose by EUR 1 billion to EUR 15 billion. Public administration debt increased by EUR 2.7 billion to EUR 129.5 billion.

data.title: Romania’s PM-designate Luca Niculescu unveils cabinet and governing strategy for parliamentary approval
data.description: Composed predominantly of Social Democratic Party (PSD) ministers and based on the Social Democrats’ governing strategy, the government led by Luca Niculescu has secured provisional support from the Liberal Party (PNL), Hungarian party UDMR, MPs representing national minorities and several smaller parliamentary factions. The investiture schedule includes hearings for ministerial candidates in the parliamentary committees on October 19-20, followed by a final vote in a joint session of the two chambers scheduled for 14:00 on October 20. Subject to a final decision by the PNL expected later on October 16, the proposed government reportedly has a solid majority of 270-300 votes, compared with the 233 required. “Most likely, Romania will have a government on Tuesday,” president Nicușor Dan said after the political parties reached an agreement in principle on approving the government. Governing strategy aligned with fiscal consolidation and reforms in public administration and state-owned enterprises. As outlined by PM-designate Luca Niculescu, the governing strategy appears aligned with the targets of fiscal consolidation and reforms in public administration and state-owned enterprises (SOEs). The government pledges to adhere to the deficit trajectory, targeting a deficit of 5.2% of GDP in 2027, maintain the flat tax rate, and list minority stakes in SOEs. Its programme includes a revision of the 2026 budget within 30 days, a 2027 budget consistent with the deficit target of 5.2% of GDP, compared with an estimated 6.2% this year, and adoption of the Wage Law for the budgetary sector in 2027. The strategy also promises restraint in social spending, with targeted support prioritised for low-income households. Wages in the budgetary sector and pensions are to be indexed in January 2027, within the limits imposed by the Excessive Deficit Procedure (EDP). Regarding pensions, the government programme pledges to keep social assistance below the ceiling of 12.2% of GDP. Pension indexation starting in 2027, alongside targeted support measures, is intended to preserve the purchasing power of pensioners, particularly those on low pensions, and other vulnerable groups. The measures are presented as consistent with the fiscal-budgetary strategy, with their impact to be calculated by the Ministry of Labour and checked jointly with the Ministry of Finance before the budget is drawn up. No other social rights are to be indexed above nominal GDP growth. Personnel expenditure is to follow the multiannual fiscal consolidation trajectory, declining from 9.3% of GDP in 2024 to 7.9% in 2031. Implementation of the unitary wage law is to respect this ceiling. Available fiscal space will be used to correct structural inequities in the wage system rather than finance uniform increases that would deepen them. Social measures, outlined both in general terms and through specific proposals – including waiving health insurance contributions for mothers on maternity leave and war veterans – have been included to balance what otherwise resembles the governing strategy of the dismissed Ilie Bolojan cabinet. Even so, these measures are conditional on identifying sufficient fiscal space to implement them without increasing the budget deficit. “The government proposes eliminating the social health insurance contribution for mothers with children under two years old, the measure being conditioned on the identification of sources of financing or compensatory savings,” the strategy states. The government team largely comprises former Social Democrat ministers. The team proposed by PM-designate Niculescu includes several former Social Democrat ministers whose past records have attracted criticism, including Marian Neacșu, who received a suspended sentence of 10.5 years for conflict of interest in 2016, and justice minister Radu Marinescu, who has been accused of plagiarism in his PhD thesis. Other appointments have raised questions about ministerial competence, including those of agriculture minister Florin Barbu and environment minister Natalia Intotero. Economy minister Daniel-Cătălin Zamfir has stood out for his rhetoric and for drafting legislation targeting banks, private companies and foreign investors. Finance minister Alexandru Nazare is keeping his post, which is likely to reassure sovereign investors about the country’s fiscal strategy, while former energy minister Bogdan Ivan is being replaced.

data.title: Wizz Air temporarily moves Timișoara flights to Arad
data.description: Wizz Air confirmed that it will temporarily relocate its flights to and from Timișoara to Arad International Airport between November 2 and 22. The carrier said the move would allow it to maintain international connections for Timișoara and the surrounding region in western Romania during the airport’s temporary closure. The airline said that it updated its booking system and notified affected passengers, who have received revised flight schedules. “Passengers who booked directly through Wizz Air are advised to check their email and confirm the changes to their travel plans to ensure their reservation is up to date. Those who booked through a travel agency, including an online agency, should contact the respective provider for further details,” reads the official announcement. There will be several exceptions during the relocation period, the company also said. On November 2, flights to Dortmund and Memmingen/Munich West will depart from Timișoara but return to Arad. Then, on November 22, flights arriving from Rome Fiumicino and Bari will land in Timișoara. All other Wizz Air flights that day will operate entirely from Arad. Representatives of Timișoara’s “Traian Vuia” Airport, one of Romania’s most important regional hubs, announced back in July that all flights will be suspended between November 2 and November 22 due to repair works on the takeoff and landing runway.

data.title: ING Bank Romania reports 15,000 accounts on newly launched investment platform as interest in investing grows
data.description: A total of 15,000 customers have opened an investment account through ING Invest, less than a month after its launch, ING Bank Romania said. The lender’s investment platform is available through its mobile app, and offers access to shares of companies listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange and major European stock exchanges, as well as Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) managed by asset management companies such as Amundi, BlackRock and Goldman Sachs Asset Management, among others. In the coming period, the bank plans to add direct access to the US market, currently available through ETFs listed on European exchanges, and the state bonds Fidelis. The platform available in Romania is the solution used by ING at group level, where ING has more than 5.3 million clients who use investment accounts. “Our ambition is to bring investing closer to people by integrating it directly into ING Home’Bank, allowing customers to take their first steps with greater confidence in a familiar digital environment. We see investing as a natural part of a modern banking relationship, and we remain committed to developing solutions that help our customers achieve their long-term financial goals,” Mihai Lazăr, Tribe Lead Investments, ING Bank Romania, said. Investment interest on the rise among Romanian savers, survey finds The launch of ING Invest comes amid increasing interest in investment products, the lender said. According to a survey conducted by iSense Solutions for ING Bank Romania in September 2026, 40% of urban residents who already save money currently hold at least one investment product. The potential for further growth remains significant: 17% of non-investors say they intend to start investing within the next 12 months, while a further 49% are open to investing in the future. Nevertheless, several perceptions continue to discourage people from entering the investment market, many of which highlight the need for greater financial education. A total of 51% of respondents believe that investing requires monitoring financial markets on a daily basis, while 48% consider advanced financial knowledge a prerequisite. The survey was conducted by iSense Solutions on behalf of ING Bank Romania between September 9 and 16, among a sample of 804 urban residents aged 18 to 65 who save money. Of the total respondents, 319 currently hold investments, while 485 do not currently invest. A previous ING Research study found that only 29% of Romanians currently invest in stocks , bonds, mutual funds, or ETFs, compared with 41% across Europe. At the same time, 30% of respondents in Romania say they have never invested but might do so in the future. It came as more than half of the Romanian respondents (51%) found it difficult or barely managed to cover their current expenses, a higher percentage than the European average (44%). The launch of the platform marks ING’s reentry into the investment segment, Mihaela Bîtu, CEO of ING Bank Romania, explained. ING Barings, the group’s brokerage company, was present in Romania from the late 1990s to the 2008 financial crisis. “I am glad that we are now returning, in a new formula, through a platform that allows us to make investments accessible to as many people as possible,” she explained. “The recent years have shown us that the potential is there, and that the investment appetite is on the rise,” she added. Established in 1994, ING Bank Romania, part of ING Group, is currently a universal bank, offering products and services to all categories of customers: large and small companies, financial institutions, small entrepreneurs and individuals. The bank has over 2 million customers in three business segments: individuals, SMEs & Mid-Corporate companies, and Wholesale Banking.

The potential for further growth remains significant: 17% of non-investors say they intend to start investing within the next 12 months, while a further 49% are open to investing in the future. Nevertheless, several perceptions continue to discourage people from entering the investment market, many of which highlight the need for greater financial education. A total of 51% of respondents believe that investing requires monitoring financial markets on a daily basis, while 48% consider advanced financial knowledge a prerequisite. The survey was conducted by iSense Solutions on behalf of ING Bank Romania between September 9 and 16, among a sample of 804 urban residents aged 18 to 65 who save money. Of the total respondents, 319 currently hold investments, while 485 do not currently invest. A previous ING Research study found that only 29% of Romanians currently invest in stocks , bonds, mutual funds, or ETFs, compared with 41% across Europe. At the same time, 30% of respondents in Romania say they have never invested but might do so in the future. It came as more than half of the Romanian respondents (51%) found it difficult or barely managed to cover their current expenses, a higher percentage than the European average (44%). The launch of the platform marks ING’s reentry into the investment segment, Mihaela Bîtu, CEO of ING Bank Romania, explained. ING Barings, the group’s brokerage company, was present in Romania from the late 1990s to the 2008 financial crisis. “I am glad that we are now returning, in a new formula, through a platform that allows us to make investments accessible to as many people as possible,” she explained. “The recent years have shown us that the potential is there, and that the investment appetite is on the rise,” she added. Established in 1994, ING Bank Romania, part of ING Group, is currently a universal bank, offering products and services to all categories of customers: large and small companies, financial institutions, small entrepreneurs and individuals. The bank has over 2 million customers in three business segments: individuals, SMEs & Mid-Corporate companies, and Wholesale Banking.

data.title: BAD: Gregor Schneider exhibition to open in Bucharest next week
data.description: BAD , an exhibition by Gregor Schneider, will open at the National Museum of Art of Romania (MNAR) next week. Gregor Schneider is one of Germany’s best-known contemporary artists. A professor at the Kunstakademie Düsseldorf, he was awarded the Golden Lion at the Venice Biennale for his work Totes Haus u r, presented at the German Pavilion in 2001, which sparked strong reactions worldwide. Since then, his controversial and provocative yet consistently rigorous and highly influential works, events, performances, and installations have addressed pressing artistic, social, historical, and political issues in locations around the world, the organizers explain. BAD is a spatial installation comprising five identical, interconnected bathrooms installed on the ground floor of the National Gallery, in MNAR’s Știrbei Building. Their dimensions, design, sanitary fixtures, lighting, and every other detail are exactly the same. “They reflect contemporary notions of cleanliness, comfort, accessibility, and seamless functionality. And yet it is precisely this seemingly effortless availability that presents a problem, turning the bathrooms into a trap-like mechanism, much like any comfortable, readily available solution to a need that gradually becomes a compulsive habit.” The exhibition explores “how each of us is trapped in the echo chamber of our own habits, thoughts, and surroundings.” The Bucharest exhibition runs in parallel with the major exhibition Gregor Schneider: Haus u r 2026 at Kunsthalle Düsseldorf, which is on view until January 2027. The partnership between the two organizing institutions, MNAR and Kunsthalle Düsseldorf, is underscored by the live-streamed video installation Haus u r, presented at MNAR at the entrance to the temporary exhibition spaces. The installation maintains a continuous, simultaneous connection between Haus u r and the exhibitions in Düsseldorf and Bucharest. The exhibition, curated by Erwin Kessler, is on view between October 24 and March 14, 2027.

data.title: The country's largest light park opens on 16 October in Bucharest, at the Botanical Garden
data.description: Lumina Park, the international concept of outdoor light trails, opens for the first time in Romania on 16 October, at the "Dimitrie Brandza" Botanical Garden of the University of Bucharest. The first local edition, "Around the World", transforms the garden after nightfall into an exploration experience for all ages, built from light, music, set design and play. Until January 2027, the public is invited to follow a night-time trail inspired by places, traditions and stories from different corners of the world. Lumina Park offers an evening experience for families, couples and groups of friends, built around the joy of exploring together. A journey around the world The international concept arrives in Bucharest as an outdoor multimedia experience. The trail is approximately 1.5 kilometres long and brings together more than 200 light installations, sets and scenes that recreate the atmosphere of destinations from around the world. Music, set design and light complete each area and tie the experience together into a single story. The "Around the World" theme offers a playful way to explore the world. Along the trail, visitors discover stories, traditions and important moments in the history of different countries. For children, the journey also becomes an adventure full of characters and landmarks that have shaped the history of the places represented, in an accessible and easy-to-follow format. A new way to discover the "Dimitrie Brandza" Botanical Garden of the University of Bucharest Lumina Park offers a different perspective on the "Dimitrie Brandza" Botanical Garden. After nightfall, the alleys become part of a carefully designed trail, and nature, art, music and play come together in an immersive experience that unfolds step by step. Visitors can walk the trail at their own pace, and a visit takes around an hour. Each area brings a new stop: an interactive installation, a set inspired by another culture, a specific soundtrack or a backdrop made for photographs. Children can look for clues along the trail and take part in an interactive online quiz, open to everyone, with prizes for those who complete it. Throughout the trail, food and beverage stands await visitors with hot drinks and snacks, perfect for cool evenings. Set outdoors, Lumina Park is the ideal alternative to an autumn or winter evening spent at home. Opening hours and tickets Lumina Park can be visited from Tuesday to Sunday, from 18:00 to 22:00, with last entry at 21:00. During the opening weekend, 16 to 18 October, Lumina Park offers special prices with 50% discounts: tickets start from RON 30. For the rest of the season, standard prices start from RON 59. The full schedule, prices for each category and ticket purchases are available at lumina-park.ro . Lumina Park, an international concept, premieres in Romania Lumina Park comes to Romania for the first time through a partnership with Universum Events, a Romanian organiser of large-scale events. The Bucharest edition, produced entirely by Universum Events, introduces a new way of spending evenings in the city, in which a walk through the Botanical Garden becomes a journey of exploration and shared experience. Present in Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic and Lithuania, Lumina Park has so far attracted more than 2.9 million visitors internationally. Across Europe, Lumina parks have explored different themes over time, adapted to each city and each season, from fantasy tales to worlds inspired by film, history or travel. "We wanted 'Around the World' to turn an ordinary evening into an adventure. Children can set off on an adventure with characters and stories from all over the world, while adults can enjoy the Botanical Garden in a way they rarely get to see it. Together with the Lumina Park team, we are bringing to Romania an international format that combines visual spectacle, play and the joy of discovering something new at every step." said Cristian Hossu, CEO of Universum Events.

data.title: Romanian literature: Lavinia Branişte’s novel Camping shortlisted for Prix Médicis étranger
data.description: Lavinia Braniște’s novel Camping has been shortlisted for this year’s Médicis Prize/ Prix Médicis, one of France’s top literary awards, in the Foreign Fiction category. The novel has been translated into French by Sylvain Audet-Găinar and was published by Éditions des Syrtes. Other Romanian writers previously shortlisted for the prize include Norman Manea, who won the Prix Médicis étranger in 2006 for Le Retour du hooligan : une vie/The Hooligan's Return and Mircea Cărtărescu, who was shortlisted for Solenoid in 2019 and Theodoros in 2024. Lavinia Braniște was born in 1983 in Brăila. She studied foreign languages and literature in Cluj-Napoca and Bucharest. Her work includes the poetry volume Povești cu mine (2006), the short story volumes Cinci minute pe zi (2011) and Escapada (2014), the children’s series Rostogol , and the novels Interior zero (2016), S onia ridică mâna (2019), Mă găseşti când vrei (2021), and Camping (2025), among others. The nominated novel, Camping , follows Sofia, a Romanian woman who lives and works at a campsite in Spain, as she plans her return home as she approaches retirement. The awards will be handed out on November 2. The jury of the Prix Médicis, chaired by playwright and novelist Pascale Roze, is composed of Marianne Alphant, Michel Braudeau, Marie Darrieussecq, Dominique Fernandez, Anne F. Garréta, Patrick Grainville, Andreï Makine, and Alain Veinstein. At the beginning of November, they vote by secret ballot for their chosen candidate until one of them obtains a majority. In the event of a tie, the president's vote counts double from the seventh round onward. The Prix Médicis was founded in 1958 by Gala Barbisan and Jean-Pierre Giraudoux as a nod to “audacious and innovative literary works” by authors whose "fame does not yet match their talent.”

data.title: VR project invites public to explore history of downtown Bucharest square
data.description: A virtual reality project hosted by the National Museum of History of Romania (MNIR) this weekend invites the public to explore two distinct periods in the history of the same area: the Royal Palace Square during the time of monarchy, and the area’s transformation during the communist period and amid the events of December 1989. Visitors can see how the architecture, symbols, urban atmosphere, and the way people related to this place changed from one era to another. The first experience explores Bucharest during the monarchy, focusing on the Palace Square, its architectural landmarks, the equestrian statue of King Carol I, and details that help visitors understand the atmosphere and everyday life of the period. Rendering of the building of the Royal Palace Illustration: Artbyte The second experience focuses on the transformations brought about by the communist period and on Revolution Square in the context of the events of 1989, presenting them as a historical moment worth learning about, researching, and discussing with younger generations, the initiators of the project explained. A view of Revolution Square with the Memorial of Rebirth Illustration: Artbyte The VR experiences were created through a process combining historical research, visual research, 3D modeling and reconstruction, 2D graphics, digital development, and audio design. The result allows visitors to immerse themselves in the space and observe how this part of Bucharest has changed over time. Portraits of communist leaders displayed in the square  Illustration: Artbyte “We didn’t want to turn VR into a history lesson, but to give people the chance to look at a familiar place through different eyes. When you see the proportions, buildings, details, and atmosphere of a particular era, questions arise naturally – and that’s exactly where the conversation about history begins,” Nicoleta-Geanina Ciubotaru, the president of the Artbyte Association and the project coordinator, explained. A view of the building of the Central University Library  Illustration: Artbyte The public can explore the two VR experiences on October 17, between 11:00 and 16:00, at MNIR. Access is free.

data.title: Lumina Park opens at Bucharest Botanical Garden
data.description: Lumina Park will make its Romanian debut on October 16 at the Dimitrie Brândză Botanical Garden in Bucharest. The outdoor multimedia experience will remain open through January 2027. Titled Around the World , the first local edition combines light installations, music, themed sets, and interactive activities. Visitors can explore the trail at their own pace, with a complete visit expected to take about one hour, representatives said. Each section is inspired by a different culture or destination and includes its own visual setting and soundtrack. Children can search for clues along the route and participate in an online interactive quiz. “We wanted Around the World to transform an ordinary evening into an adventure,” said Cristian Hossu, CEO of Romanian organizer Universum Events. “Together with the Lumina Park team, we are bringing an international format to Romania that combines visual spectacle, play, and the joy of discovering something new at every step.” The park will be open Tuesday through Sunday from 6 p.m. to 10 p.m., with the last admission at 9 p.m. During the opening weekend, October 16-18, tickets will be offered at a 50% discount, with prices starting at RON 30. Standard prices for the remainder of the season will start at RON 59. Further details can be found here . Lumina Park currently operates in Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, and Lithuania and has attracted more than 2.9 million visitors internationally.

data.title: Nearly half of Romanians start Christmas shopping on Black Friday, survey says
data.description: Romanian shoppers start their Christmas shopping early, according to research conducted by Shopfully, a European drive-to-store solutions provider operating in 25 countries. Around 42% of Romanians start Christmas shopping on Black Friday, November 6, when they look for gifts at better prices. Meanwhile, 18% will start planning their shopping during October, and only 11% will leave their shopping until the last minute, in December. By contrast, 14% of participants say they have not planned any Christmas purchases this year. According to the same survey, Romanians prefer physical stores when looking for Christmas gifts, with six in ten saying they intend to shop this way, while 28% choose a mix of online and offline shopping, and only 11% prefer to shop exclusively online. When it comes to discovering offers and gift ideas, 41% indicated digital catalogs and online brochures. Printed catalogs were mentioned by 29%, while 27% prefer to find inspiration directly in stores, and 21% of shoppers browse retailers’, brands’, and e-commerce platforms’ websites. “For some shoppers, Black Friday and Christmas are not two separate moments, but stages of the same shopping period. Offers discovered online can influence which stores they choose to visit, and retailers need relevant, easy-to-find communication, including at the local level. It is important for them to be present during the research stage, not just at the moment of purchase,” said Cătălin Pațachia, Shopfully Country Manager. The same survey shows that artificial intelligence has become a shopping assistant and a tool for comparing prices as well as finding the best offers. As such, 35% of respondents are considering using artificial intelligence when researching purchases. By contrast, the same percentage of shoppers still prefer not to use any AI tools and to find the stores and products they need on their own. Although most people know how to use artificial intelligence, almost 20% say they are still unfamiliar with these tools for shopping assistance. This year, the Black Friday budget is estimated at around RON 1,000 by nearly half of the study participants, while 29% do not have a fixed budget, and 10% say they do not want to spend any money. For Christmas gifts and Black Friday offers, Romanians choose clothing, footwear, and accessories, as well as home goods, decorations, and furniture. Each of these categories was mentioned by 35% of study participants, while food and beverages were chosen by 31%, children's toys by 22%, and 20% said they would buy new electronic products, phones, laptops, televisions, or smart devices. The Shopfully study was conducted in October 2026 on a representative sample of respondents from Romania.

data.title: Weekend calendar: National Theater Festival, KINOdiseea, Taste of Transylvania, Titan Pumpkin Fest, Astra Film Festival
data.description: In Bucharest: National Theater Festival October 16 - October 25 For ten days, the festival brings 36 productions in the official selection, with 88 performances in 24 halls, along with over 50 other events, hosted in 28 other cultural spaces in Bucharest. More details here . KINOdiseea Until October 18 The 18th edition of the international film festival for young audiences will hold screenings at the Gloria Hall, the Romanian Peasant Museum Cinema and the Armenian Cultural Center. The program includes international films and animations, shows, street art, and various workshops. More here . Bucharest Photofest Until October 18 The festival presents around 50 events across more than ten venues in Bucharest, with over 200 exhibiting artists. The program covers exhibitions, film screenings, a conference, analogue photography, a photobook fair, educational events and concerts. More details here . Art Safari Until December 20 The new season presents an exhibition about Brâncuși and the muses that influenced his creation, one about the Pop Art movement; photographs by Cristian Mungiu; as well as a series of other temporary exhibitions. More details here . Wild Metaphysics Until October 24 The exhibition, open at Gaep, features six Brazilian artists whose works explore the extraordinary, the oneiric, and the metaphysical. The artists, whose work is presented in Romania for the first time, are Thiago Barbalho, Maria Nepomuceno, Mariana Rocha, Guga Szabzon, Marina Woisky, Michel Zózimo. More here . Taste of Transylvania October 16 – October 18 Held at Dimitrie Gusti Village Museum, the event showcases the gastronomic heritage of Transylvania as it meets contemporary cuisine. A total of 36 restaurants, beverage brands and gastronomic concepts, including two restaurants with Michelin stars and some of the best restaurants in Romania, await visitors. The program includes culinary demonstrations, free workshops, tastings and live music. More details here . Titan Pumpkin Fest October 16 – October 18 Held in Titan Park, the event dedicated to autumn awaits visitors with creative workshops, shows, concerts and activities for children. Entry is free. In the country: Picasso en visite Until January 17, 2027 The exhibition, presented by Art Encounters in Timișoara in partnership with Musée Picasso Antibes, brings together 69 works by Pablo Picasso, namely paintings, drawings, engravings, lithographs and ceramics, presented for the first time to the Romanian public. More here . BETA – Timișoara Architecture Biennial Until October 25 The event takes place under the theme “In Practice – as opposed to ‘in theory’” and will see more than 40 projects by participants from 15 countries transform the building of the former Ion Mincu High School. More here . Astra Film Festival October 17 – October 25 The festival, which takes place in Sibiu, runs a program of documentary films, conversations with filmmakers and guests, debates and meetings with audiences of all ages, as well as a special section dedicated to students. More details here .
