data.title: Romanian court lifts seizure on Nordis properties in Mamaia worth over EUR 100 million
data.description: Judges at the Bucharest Court of Appeal admitted the appeals filed by infamous real estate developer Nordis Management SRL and Nordis Mamaia SRL and ordered the lifting of the precautionary measures previously imposed by DIICOT prosecutors on Thursday, October 15. The decision concerns the residential and hotel complex in Mamaia, whose premises and apartments had been placed under seizure in July 2026 as part of the criminal investigation into the company. The total value of the real estate assets released from seizure exceeds EUR 100 million. Despite this ruling, the legal situation of the individuals involved in the case remains unchanged, according to G4Media . The judges of the Bucharest Court of Appeal rejected as unfounded the appeal filed by Vladimir Ciorbă against the same order issued by anti-mafia prosecutors. Consequently, the precautionary seizure imposed on his assets and personal wealth remains in place. The Nordis case handled by the Prosecutor's Office attached to the High Court of Cassation and Justice – DIICOT concerns suspicions of forming an organised criminal group and other economic crimes. The criminal investigation is continuing, and the lifting of the seizure on the companies' assets allows administrative or commercial procedures concerning the respective properties to resume, without halting the investigations conducted by prosecutors. Earlier this month, prosecutors announced they had extended the criminal investigation against former Social Democratic parliamentarian Laura Vicol in the Nordis case, charging her with continued false statements, continued money laundering, and complicity in fraud. Background In February 2025, Nordis owners Emanuel Poștoacă and Vladimir Ciorbă, the latter's wife, former PSD MP Laura Vicol, and others were detained by DIICOT on charges including forming an organized criminal group, embezzlement, money laundering, tax evasion, and fraud. They allegedly collected EUR 195 million from Nordis clients, people who wanted to buy apartments in residential complexes developed by Nordis and paid in advance, and embezzled more than EUR 70 million. The arrests were later overturned by the Romanian High Court . In August, the Bucharest Court of Appeal lifted almost EUR 90 million in asset seizures imposed by prosecutors on real estate assets, as well as on the accounts and shares held by Nordis owners Vladimir Ciorbă, Florin Alexandru Poștoacă, legal director Camelia Bîndiu and the group's parent company, Nordis Management. Around the same time, prosecutors expanded the investigation into Nordis. Subsequently, the prosecutor reimposed seizures on Nordis apartments worth more than EUR 64 million. The seizure was confirmed by the court on November 14, 2025.

data.title: City Grill invests EUR 500,000 in first Hanu’ Berarilor restaurant outside Bucharest
data.description: City Grill, a leading Romanian-owned restaurant group, announced that it opened its fourth Hanu’ Berarilor restaurant following a EUR 500,000 investment. The venue in Cluj-Napoca, in the Transylvania region, is the brand’s first location outside Bucharest. The restaurant is located in the building known as the Mikes Palace, which was built around 1800 in the city’s Old Town. It has 240 seats across the interior and inner courtyard, 50 in the vaulted wine cellar, and 100 on the terrace overlooking the square. “The first Hanu’ Berarilor outside Bucharest could only open in a spectacular setting, and the Mikes Palace in the heart of Cluj-Napoca is exactly that kind of place,” said Daniel Mischie, executive chairman of City Grill Group. The palace is attributed to architect Joseph Leder, who also designed the Teleki Palace and the Reformed College. Its features include a vaulted passageway and an inner courtyard with two levels of Baroque galleries. City Grill has previously opened Hanu’ Berarilor restaurants in three historic Bucharest buildings, namely Casa Oprea Soare in 2009, Casa Elena Lupescu in 2011, and Uranus in 2019. “Fitting out a restaurant in a historic monument can cost up to twice as much as in an ordinary building, but it pays off in the long run through the uniqueness of the venue and its status as a tourist destination,” Daniel Mischie said. The group entered the Cluj-Napoca market in October 2024 by acquiring a majority stake in Marty Restaurants, which operates six venues in the city. Including Hanu’ Berarilor, City Grill’s local capacity now exceeds 1,700 seats. City Grill Group reported consolidated revenue of EUR 90 million in 2025 and is targeting EUR 100 million in 2026. The company has allocated EUR 6.5 million for investments this year and is also adding Cluj’s Chios restaurant to its portfolio while retaining its existing brand. The group operates the Caru cu Bere, Hanu lui Manuc, Hanu’ Berarilor, Peșcaruș, Buongiorno.Italian, City Grill, City Grill Family, Marty Restaurants and Aubergine brands, as well as the La Boheme hotel.

data.title: Romanian entrepreneurs take over Gazprom’s 19 gas stations in Romania
data.description: Two Romanian entrepreneurs, Iulian Stanciu and Adrian Crețoiu, have indirectly taken over the Gazprom gas station network in Romania from NIS Petrol, the local subsidiary of Serbia’s largest oil company, Naftna Industrija Srbije (NIS), which is still indirectly controlled by Russia through Gazprom and Gazprom Neft. Specifically, NIS Petrol was acquired by Romanian metal construction company Argenta SRL, owned by businessmen Adrian Crețoiu (60%) and Iulian Stanciu, the former head of eMAG (40%), according to a decision by the Competition Council approving the transaction cited by Economica . Stanciu and Crețoiu also control Foraj Sonde Videle (BVB: FOJE), which last month took over Raffles Energy, a UK holding company that owns two Romanian companies active in the energy sector, particularly in natural gas and electricity production. The information that Gazprom gas stations in Romania had changed ownership emerged as early as July, in the company’s report, but it did not make clear who the buyer was. Oil company NIS was subjected to US sanctions because of its Russian shareholders, Gazprom Neft and Gazprom, which owned 44.9% and 11.3% of NIS shares, respectively. However, the Russian companies had to sell their stakes. NIS, which operates 19 gas stations in Romania, announced its withdrawal from Bulgaria and Romania last year due to the challenges facing its operations in these markets. The company, which is undergoing preventive concordat proceedings, ended 2025 with a turnover of RON 205.5 million and a loss of RON 95 million. The company also has a portfolio of six oil and gas perimeters under concession in western Romania, where it acts as the operator.

data.title: Romania’s Culture Ministry revives study, creative scholarships after two decades
data.description: Romania’s Ministry of Culture is set to re-establish the mobility fund for study and creative scholarships starting in 2027, after almost two decades. Each scholarship will be worth RON 10,000 (EUR 1,873), and the funding can also be used for training, travel, artistic residencies, and creative activities. According to the initiative, study scholarships include scholarships themselves, training placements, travel grants, and artistic residencies. Creative scholarships, in turn, are intended for carrying out creative activities in the cultural fields. The regulation establishes 11 fields for which scholarships may be awarded: performing arts, cinematographic art, audiovisual arts, visual arts, art curation and criticism, music and musicology, written culture, intangible cultural heritage, movable cultural heritage, architecture, intercultural dialogue, and cultural diplomacy. The fields may be further detailed or adjusted according to the priorities established each year. The amount awarded by each scholarship may subsequently be amended by order of the Minister of Culture, depending on the budget approved each year. The money must be used exclusively for the purpose for which the funding was granted. Beneficiaries will be selected based on evaluation criteria approved annually by order of the Minister of Culture, according to G4Media . According to the regulation, applicants must submit, among other documents, an application form, a CV, a copy of their identity card or passport, documents concerning relevant studies, a letter of intent, and a study or creative project. The application file must also contain at least two letters of recommendation from specialists in the field, as well as a declaration concerning the documents submitted and compliance with the eligibility requirements. Documents will be submitted online, and incomplete or late applications will be rejected. Employees of the Ministry of Culture and institutions under its authority or coordination, as well as certain relatives of these employees, are not eligible for these scholarships while their employment or service relationships remain in effect, according to the regulation. The funding will be awarded through a contract concluded between the Ministry of Culture and the beneficiary. The contract will establish the purpose of the scholarship, its amount and payment method, duration, reporting obligations, and the conditions under which the money may be recovered. Beneficiaries must submit documents demonstrating that the funded activities have been carried out. For travel grants and artistic residencies, for example, documents concerning transportation and accommodation may be requested. For scholarships lasting more than three months, an interim report is also required. Failure to comply with reporting obligations or using the money for a purpose other than the one approved may lead to contract termination and recovery of the amounts awarded.

data.title: Romanian president highlights Bucharest green belt in sustainable development message
data.description: Romanian president Nicușor Dan called for nature protection to be permanently integrated into public policy and economic development in his opening message to the Climate Change Summit 2026 on Wednesday, October 14. The message was delivered at the Palace of Parliament by state adviser Ștefania-Georgiana Simion. President Dan said Romania needs secure and affordable energy, investment, and infrastructure adapted to climate change, while also protecting the forests, water, and habitats on which public health and well-being depend. “Protecting natural heritage is part of the state’s responsibility toward its citizens, a priority that I support and want to see reflected in public decisions,” he said. The president identified the Bucharest-Ilfov Green Belt project as an example of cooperation among citizens, specialists, and authorities. “Protecting the forests around the capital and restoring connections between natural areas have a direct impact on residents’ quality of life,” he stated. “They must be included in the planning of a metropolitan area that needs cleaner air, recreational spaces, and better adaptation to high temperatures.” Back in October 2023, while serving as Bucharest mayor, Nicușor Dan signed the Memorandum for Clean Air, Health and the Future , the founding document of the Bucharest-Ilfov Green Belt and the wider national green belt initiative. This was promoted by the Centura Verde/Green Belt Foundation, an initiative of mountaineer and conservationist Alex Gǎvan. In his message on Wednesday, president Dan also advocated a development model for Roșia Montană that protects the landscape and cultural heritage while creating opportunities for residents. He said the area demonstrated the importance of involving citizens in decisions that could irreversibly change their communities. Moreover, the president called for stable support for centers that rehabilitate injured and orphaned wildlife and urged authorities to clarify how Lake Techirghiol’s protected status is being observed in land-use decisions and local activities. “Protecting nature must be permanently integrated into any vision for development,” Nicușor Dan said. “That means predictable rules, rigorous assessments, and resources for conservation.” The Green Belt is meant to be the largest green infrastructure project in Romania, Alex Gǎvan says. Mountaineer and conservationist Alex Găvan, founder of the Green Belt Foundation, addressed the Climate Change Summit’s Green Stage on Wednesday, October 14. He said during his intervention at the Restoring the Balance Sheet: Nature as Europe's Next Critical Infrastructure event that the proposed network should integrate forests, water, wetlands, grasslands, and farmland around and within cities, rather than operate as a conventional green belt primarily intended to limit construction. "Bucharest and Romania need the right mechanisms to successfully face the challenges of the 21st century. Green belts are such a mechanism - and the Green Belt is meant to be the largest green infrastructure project in Romania,” he said. “It should be planned, financed, and managed like other types of infrastructure, such as roads, utilities, and energy networks.” Alex Gǎvan talks about the Green Belt at Climate Change Summit 2026 event; credit:  FotografulTAU The initiative has already secured protection from commercial logging for more than 26,000 hectares of forest in Ilfov County through Romania’s new Forestry Code . The Green Belt Foundation is now in an ongoing process with the Environment Ministry "to accomplish through the implementing rules of the Forestry Code the protection from commercial logging" of several hundred thousand hectares of publicly owned forests surrounding Romanian cities. A proposed second stage would establish a national financing program that municipalities could voluntarily access to develop full green belts. “We have also taken the project to Brussels, aiming to scale it up across the EU. Because protection without financing is a promise - and financing without protection is a subsidy that evaporates. Romania and Europe need both,” Alex Găvan stated. He further argued that the economic value of standing forests is largely absent from public budgets, despite the services they provide. “Over 70% of Europe’s economy depends on nature, yet we value it at zero. In public budgets, a road is counted as an investment. A forest is counted only as timber. The value of a standing forest - in terms of clean air, cooler summers, and flood protection - appears nowhere,” he said. “And in the next EU budget, nature loses even its own dedicated line: it is merged into a single pot for climate and the environment, accounting for 35% of the budget.” Further on, Alex Găvan also presented the Green Belt as an economic and public health investment, arguing that decision-makers are more likely to prioritize green infrastructure when its benefits are expressed in financial terms. He said said air pollution costs Bucharest around EUR 6 billion a year, “the highest bill of any city in the European Union” - one paid through hospital admissions, lost working days, and lives. He also cited public data suggesting that residents could gain more than four years in life expectancy if authorities met their pollution-reduction targets. In this context, Gǎvan described a green belt as “one of the cheapest utilities we can build to bring down that bill.” According to him, green infrastructure should receive the same legal status, multiyear financing, and long-term planning as conventional infrastructure. “Roads connect cities, but I truly believe that green belts keep them livable,” Alex Găvan concluded. “Planning one without the other isn’t infrastructure planning; it’s half a plan.”

data.title: World Class Romania opens EUR 3 mln fitness club at One High District
data.description: World Class Romania, a major player in the health & fitness industry in the country, announced the opening of its club at the One High District complex in Bucharest, developed with a EUR 3 million investment. According to the company, the new club was developed to bring fitness, assessment, recovery, wellness and longevity solutions together in a single concept. This shaped every part of the club, from design, equipment selection and space planning to the services and experience offered to members. The new club is located within the One High District residential development in Bucharest. The investment was funded by a capital contribution from its shareholder, Vectr Holdings. “The investment responds both to the potential of a fast-developing area and to changing consumer expectations. Today, members want services that help them understand their bodies better, train effectively, recover well and invest in their long-term health. We built this club around those needs, bringing together our infrastructure, technology and team expertise into a cohesive fitness, recovery and longevity experience,” said Matei Filipidescu, CEO of World Class Romania. The training, recovery and relaxation areas have been organized into one unified concept, with a focus on functionality, comfort and an intuitive experience for members. For training, the club offers dedicated Pilates Reformer, Booty Builder and HYROX zones and a group fitness studio, alongside high-performance equipment for cardio, strength and functional training. Aquatic and recovery facilities feature two cold plunge tubs, a semi-Olympic swimming pool with four lanes, a dry sauna and a steam room. The club also has a dedicated children’s changing room, designed for the families who use the club. Members can park in the covered car park, with the first two hours free of charge. After members arrive, the first step is the Longevity Check, a service included in the membership that gives them an overview of their physical condition and functional abilities. The assessment combines bioimpedance analysis and motion tracking technology with cognitive and functional tests, looking at six dimensions: Body, Mobility, Balance, Mind, Strength and Cardio. Based on the results, each member receives an individual profile that includes their Wellness Age, an estimate of their functional age, and a benchmark for tracking progress over time. At the end of the assessment, they are given a personalised training plan, built on this profile and tailored to their goals. A trainer validates the plan and adjusts it along the way, while regular reassessments measure results and help refine the training on an ongoing basis. In the strength area, the club will introduce a new generation of smart equipment that uses artificial intelligence to adjust resistance, tempo, and range of motion in real time to each user's profile, fitness level, and goals. Automatic settings and digital feedback will make training more intuitive, safer and more effective. Recovery will also have its own space: the Recovery Corner, designed to help members recharge after training. The area is equipped with massage guns, compression boots and massage and relaxation chairs.

For training, the club offers dedicated Pilates Reformer, Booty Builder and HYROX zones and a group fitness studio, alongside high-performance equipment for cardio, strength and functional training. Aquatic and recovery facilities feature two cold plunge tubs, a semi-Olympic swimming pool with four lanes, a dry sauna and a steam room. The club also has a dedicated children’s changing room, designed for the families who use the club. Members can park in the covered car park, with the first two hours free of charge. After members arrive, the first step is the Longevity Check, a service included in the membership that gives them an overview of their physical condition and functional abilities. The assessment combines bioimpedance analysis and motion tracking technology with cognitive and functional tests, looking at six dimensions: Body, Mobility, Balance, Mind, Strength and Cardio. Based on the results, each member receives an individual profile that includes their Wellness Age, an estimate of their functional age, and a benchmark for tracking progress over time. At the end of the assessment, they are given a personalised training plan, built on this profile and tailored to their goals. A trainer validates the plan and adjusts it along the way, while regular reassessments measure results and help refine the training on an ongoing basis. In the strength area, the club will introduce a new generation of smart equipment that uses artificial intelligence to adjust resistance, tempo, and range of motion in real time to each user's profile, fitness level, and goals. Automatic settings and digital feedback will make training more intuitive, safer and more effective. Recovery will also have its own space: the Recovery Corner, designed to help members recharge after training. The area is equipped with massage guns, compression boots and massage and relaxation chairs.

data.title: Romania’s Dedeman replaces Praktiker signs across Greece
data.description: Stores belonging to the Praktiker Hellas chain have begun replacing their signs with the name “Dedeman,” according to moneyreview.gr . The name change, which is also accompanied by extensive renovations, is starting with the company’s flagship store in Tavros, a suburb of Athens. In the coming period, the name change and renovations will continue at the chain’s other 16 stores, a process that will take place gradually to ensure a smooth transition to the new model. The DIY (do-it-yourself) Praktiker brand first appeared in Greece in November 1991 as a subsidiary of the German group Praktiker AG. Following the bankruptcy of its German parent company, the Greek subsidiary was acquired by Prem Watsa’s Fairfax fund, without changing its name. In the summer of 2025, Praktiker Hellas came under the control of Paval Holding, the Romanian investment group controlled by the Pavăl brothers, which owns the DIY store chain Dedeman. The brand is the market leader in Romania’s DIY sector. The new owners took steps to change Praktiker Hellas’s name to Dedeman Hellas, with the initial plan envisaging that the store signs would be replaced later, starting in 2027. Changes don't stop with the name. In recent months, Dedeman Hellas has undertaken a series of other measures in an effort, on the one hand, to strengthen the company’s capital base and, on the other, to reorganize its operations and structure. During the summer, Dedeman Hellas completed the absorption of its subsidiaries Adam Logistics and Petral (formerly Southrock, whose business activity is real estate management), following two share capital increases in February and March worth a total of EUR 39 million. Changes to the supply and network management system are also underway, with the aim of improving the company’s performance and reducing operating costs. To this end, the practices followed by Paval Holding at the Romanian company Dedeman are being adapted to the Greek market, and the plan also includes introducing products under Dedeman’s own brand, manufactured at Dedeman’s factories in Romania, to stores in Greece. A crucial challenge for the new owner of Praktiker Hellas, now Dedeman Hellas, is increasing sales but, above all, returning to profitability, the Greek publication reported. In 2024, the chain’s turnover stood at EUR 186.21 million, down 0.70% from 2023. The company recorded a loss of EUR 1.76 million, compared with EUR 1.40 million in 2023. The company has not yet published its financial statements for the 2025 financial year.

data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. Documento António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13
